text: I really wanted to take my friend to Camellia's during my last visit to New Orleans but we really didn't feel like heading up town in the rain. Luckily we stumbled upon their new location purely by chance our last evening in town as we walked down Chartres on a Sunday night and tried to decide where and what we wanted to eat. I think it must stay open later than the other one too because it was definitely dinner time when were lucky enough to notice its presence about a block farther down Chartres from Napoleon House (which apparently is closed on Sunday). I know for sure it does open for breakfast at 8AM (since I asked) and they do take credit cards! This new Camellia location which opened last December seems much bigger and less cramped than the original. There is more seating, more elbow room, and the finishings seem nicer but still very quaint. I am also happy to report that the food is still outstanding. Both locations serve some of the best hamburgers I have ever had. This time I had mine with a side of onion rings and a two scoop chocolate freeze. I highly recommend the chocolate freeze. It is what a shake/malt is supposed to taste like before America got taken over by corn syrup. It's pure sugar and real chocolate and the beef in the hamburgers are of similar high quality. I hope to try breakfast here on my next sojourn in the Vieux Carre. I highly recommend this place!

I recommend this place to anyone who likes take-out, doesn't mind small spaces, and can tolerate a possible lack of service. Fantastic food!

I think they are fast and effective and the meat taste amazing every time. I mean we throw the brown bag in the recycling bag and every time our black lab pulls it out to lick it and smell it. text: So I guess all of these great reviews are for the $10 lunch buffet. Let's talk about dinner shall we? A year and a half ago my husband and I won a $100 gift certificate for this place at a fundraising event. It was clearly marked "No Exp." We're huge fans of Ekta, so when we have a hankering for Indian, we usually go there. But we were in the neighborhood last night and thought, what the heck? We were surprised to see the restaurant nearly empty. Only three other tables were seated. We enter the restaurant and stand near the host station. We wait for a few minutes as servers continue to walk around us. No one stops to say, "We'll be right with you." It's was like we were invisible. We said, "If it weren't for the gift card, we'd walk right out the door." After about five minutes we made it very apparent that we wanted a seat. I actually had to FLAG someone down. In an EMPTY restaurant, why on earth were we being ignored as we waited by the host station? Then, rather than sit us by a window, they sat us at a oddly placed table in a thoroughfare, in the back of the restaurant. Now, the place is nearly empty - why wouldn't they put patrons in the nicer seats by the windows? If anything it would make the restaurant look slightly less dead. It was 8:45PM at night - it's not like they were going to get a dinner rush at that point. Whatever. So we were finally seated about seven minutes after entering the establishment with NO apology. Nothing. I think a "Sorry for the wait" would have been in order. So we order our meal and some wine. Again, in an empty restaurant, the wine takes ten minutes to get to the table. I could have walked home and grabbed a bottle in that amount of time. We began to think, "No wonder this place is so empty." Food: I almost considered giving Palace two stars because the Naan was legit and we enjoyed the Lamb Saag. But the prices were ridiculous considering the poor service. (Again, apparently they have a cheap lunch buffet...) Each main dish was around $22-25. At Ekta, where the food blows this place out of the water, each main is $10 cheaper. In a restaurant with $20+ courses, you'd expect a more professional vibe from the staff. We were gobsmacked by the prices, and while the food was good, it was no Ekta. And at that price point, we'd never come back (without a gift certificate!) But what we experienced after we ate, pretty much sealed the deal. We hand our waiter the gift card and he looks at it oddly. Ready for it? "We don't accept these anymore." To that we said, "That's none of our concern. It's clearly noted on the card, "No exp." So then a manager is sent to our table. With NO pleasantries he barks, "When did you get this?!" We told him the event and the name of the charity and he said, "That was over two years ago!" We said, "No, actually a year and a half ago, and it's clearly marked, no expiration date." So he leaves in a gruff, huffing and puffing, while mumbling loud enough so we could hear how "unfair" it was and how he was going to "contact them and make them pay." (Contact the charity? That's really charitable of you, Mr. Manager!) It gets better. He comes back to the table with a receipt that he just printed saying, "This was only for $50." Oh wait a minute. We clearly ate more than $50 worth (not hard when Lamb Saag will put you back $25) knowing that we had $100 on the card. We started to argue and he literally pushed the receipt in our face. At this point he was getting really aggressive so I just gave him my credit card for the remaining $20. It doesn't stop there. Then he corners my husband after he's coming out of the bathrooms. (The bathrooms are really awkward by the way. The door to the bar faces the bathroom so while I washed my hands, bar patrons were watching. Creepy.) Anyway, he corners my husband (corners him!) and follows him back to our table and says, "This is from 2007." 2007? The event was in November 2010! In the end we said, "This is none of our concern. We won the certificate at an event. In the future, use expiration dates if you're not going to honor gifts you give to charities." He then stands over me after he handed me the credit card receipt to sign as if he wanted to see how much we'd tip them. (Right?) I look at him and say, "Excuse me, can you back off?" (I actually had to say that!) At this point, I was so tempted to do a runner and report them to the BBB. We did not leave a tip, which I have NEVER done in my life. If we get bad service I'll leave 15%, but my usual MINIMUM is 20%. I really was shocked at how this was handled. Bottom line: There is far better Indian in Philly for a fraction of the price. Don't assume that you're getting better service or a classier experience at this place for the prices. Go elsewhere. We will never go back. Notice how empty it is for dinner? There is a reason for that
label: NEG

text: One of my go-to spots. This place is really is great. An authentic (and BYO!) Brazilian churrascaria. You walk in to a cafeteria-style salad bar with plates for eating-in or taking-out. If you eat there, you can do by-the-pound or the all-you-can-eat rodizio. I usually just do by-the-pound since their prices are super cheap and I don't eat enough to justify the rodizio. But if you're up to the challenge, it's definitely worth it. From the buffet, I always grab some potato salad and a carrot/tuna/raisin/potato stick salad that's way more than the sum of it's parts. Then I move on to the hot foods section, where I mostly stick to their rice and black beans, which are also delicious and authentic. I might grab a bit of other hot foods if they look good, but really you're here for the meat that's served at the counter so don't stray! Once at the counter, load up! Be sure and grab their namesake cut of meat, picanha (top sirloin) and the pork sausages (UNREAL delicious!). Other standouts include chicken wrapped in bacon, chicken wing drumettes, and beef short ribs. Then sit down and a waitress will take your drink order. Lots of choices here. If you bring cachaca, they'll bring you the mix for different flavors of caipirinhas. But they also have some great fruit drinks and the Brazilian soda Guarana, which is actually the base for most energy drinks and kind of tastes like a sprite mixed with red bull. Very good and will help wake you up from your meat coma! If you still have room for desert, there's plenty of options though I feel like they all have coconut so not much flavor variety. All in all a fantastic spot and highly recommend it.
label: POS

text: Here's how much I liked this place: I joined Yelp specifically so I could leave an awesome review for Ciro's. I eat at a lot of high end restaurants, and this was, without a doubt, my favorite place of 2012. When we first arrived, I had a very hard time finding it. You think you're at some random apartment building--you're not. Keep looking, it's there. When you find the door, they ask you for a password like an old time speakeasy. It's all in good fun. They seated us in a little private cove with a curtain, which was very intimate. I love craft cocktails. Twice I just ordered off the menu; two other times I told them what I liked and had the bartender make me something. I was never disappointed. At many places where the cocktails are the the focus, the food goes by the wayside. That's not the case here. We really liked the Crab Avocado martini, the duck fries were great too. Everything we had was wonderful. If you're into delicious, exotic cocktails that you can't find anywhere else and great food, you're going to love Ciro's.

text: Yesterday, April 5, 2011, I took my family on a ten hour, round trip drive from kentucky to Indianapolis to have a wonderful lunch at Jersey's Cafe. This story is about my bad experience at Jersey's Cafe. My wife, two and a half year old, six month old, and I are used to eating at all types of restaurants from pizza to medium dining. The kids were having fun, not making a scene, or being overly loud. In fact, another customer commented to my wife that we had cute kids, and we shared small conversation with the table next to us. I have worked in restaurants, as has my wife. After seeing Diners, Drive-ins, and Dives, and having reviewed their online menu, I decided to try the Westwood sandwich and their chicken salad sandwich with bacon. The steak sandwich looked amazing, and I eagerly wanted to let its rich flavors of steak, tomato sauce, meatball, cheese, and crunchy crusted roll (roll is "imported" from New York) wash over my senses and transform my lunch into Nirvana. I had high expectations. Sadly, I never even saw that steak sandwich. We got there at 3pm on that Tuesday. With kids, it's always best to aim for in-between meals, just in case. Their sign warns customers of a 30 minute wait from order to food and blame their success. Ok, whatever. It's made to order, not a problem... I can wait for good food. One waitress and one new buss-person was working the 45 seat (or so) dine-in area. I let my wife order our main reason for being there, and she ordered the big blue, and I told the waitress that we would each have one (oops, this was the wrong sandwich for me, but exactly what my wife wanted). Waitress suggested getting one of the big blue's and sharing it. Neither my wife nor I wanted to share because of the specialness of the long drive and the anticipation of a wonderful sandwich. This was not the Westwood which I wanted. Probably my fault for ordering the wrong sandwich. I'll grant the Jersey cafe that, but how a restaurant handles problems is as important as how they make food. We also ordered a $3 hot dog for my 2 year old and two drinks (another $4). After waiting every bit of half an hour, they brought the sandwiches, and I immediately told the buss-person, food carrier that there must be a mistake, that I ordered the steak sandwich. He called over the waitress and I repeated that I had ordered the steak sandwich on the big roll, covered in cheese... you know. We cleared up the issue, I had mis-ordered. I asked what we could do, because I did not want the sandwich in front of me. I didn't really want to wait another 30 minutes for the other sandwich, but the waitress was clear that ANY SOLUTION WOULD REQUIRE ME TO PAY FOR THIS SANDWICH. It turns out that no manager was there that afternoon, just cooks and waitresses: no supervisor/manager to appeal to. So, I asked if she would make me pay for a sandwich that I ordered and didn't like. She said, in no uncertain terms, that if I ordered it, I'd have to pay for it, regardless of anything about the sandwich. It's an $8 sandwich. So I told her that if I had to pay for a sandwich I didn't want, regardless of what I ordered or received, her tip would be used to pay for it. She got angry, made a comment, stormed off and it sounded like she either bumped something which fell, or threw something on her way into the kitchen. At that point, any tip to her was history. She ignored/avoided us the rest of our time there. I'm not rich, and I will not pay $6-10 tip for a meal that included an unsolved problem. I understand that people are picky, and often overly picky. Jersey Cafe's policy, though, transforms an otherwise decent eat-in deli into a lunch counter. Why pay a waitress to bring my food when they really want me to order at a counter, pay, get my food and negotiate problems with them holding the money, and me holding the food. That's the problem she and the restaurant creates with such a policy. She was calm when talking about a problem with my money. When I made the problem affect her money, she got angry and emotional. Interesting, huh? If a waitress cannot solve such problems when they come up because of restaurant policy, the restaurant shouldn't have serving staff: they should have counter staff. Were this sandwich joint to have had counter staff, she wouldn't have expected a tip, she never would have gotten personally involved, and I would have probably not expected her to be able to fix that problem. But I would have still asked and hoped they would have tried something to make me happy. I don't want anything for free. I just wanted to taste that steak sandwich, but was not going to pay double. Overall for the restaurant, I didn't want my money back, I didn't want something for free. I wanted their sandwich. I would have loved to have reviewed their food here, but because of the wait staff and Jersey Cafe's policy, this review is about the restaurant, not the food. I had a bad experience.

text: In the head-to-head burger throwdown of Five Guys vs. Elevation Burger, Five Guys took 2nd place. Or last place, depending on how you look at it. Heres the greasy details... It wasnt nearly as juicy as the competition, although it was slightly better seasoned. Chalk that up to the policy of cooking everything well-done. Five Guys even uses "juicy" and "well done" in the same sentence on every menu board in their restaurants, in an effort to convice you this is possible. I respectfully disagree though, pointing to the reliance on multiple patties, melted cheese, and free toppings to create the illusion of moist, "juicy" texture. It probably doesnt matter to the masses though, as most people slather their burgers in ketchup, mayo, or whatever. However, the difference was obvious as daylight in this comparo, and should be noted. The american cheese used was plentiful and nicely melted, but lacked the exotic appeal of the vermont cheddar the competition featured. The grilled onions I had specified though were barely grilled at all, which seriously altered the flavor profile of this burger, not to mention added a crunch I didnt care for. Overall, the Five Guys burger was just OK by itself, but it was borderline disappointing when compared to the Elevation burger. After sampling both, I still wanted to go back and have another bite of that Elevation burger. In identical configurations, at identical prices, Five Guys didnt stack up to Elevation. However, while not offically considered in this comparison, Five Guys also allows a higher degree of customization with the availability of bacon and condiments like BBQ sauce - 2 things the competition lacks.

text: I feel so ashamed for having been lured into this place. Maybe I should go see a hypnotist, have the whole episode wiped from memory. I knew immediately that I'd be taking off my clothes and burning them as soon as I got home. I mean, the bar was just steeped in this putrid "leper's foot" smell. My next impression: the room looked like the bar scene from Star Wars. Holy mackerel, the clientele appeared wrecked past the point of return, ready to turn into werewolves. Crazed, sweaty-faced, babbling in incomprehensible tongues. They jigged dementedly as the cover band slogged through some pretty repulsive-sounding "Kenny Loggins" type music. The crowd was digging it, but maybe they thought they were at a Rolling Stones concert. The floors are unbelievably tacky. As in, don't stand in one place for too long, or you'll find yourself frozen there, as if in quicksand. I'm not sure if it was blood, ectoplasm, afterbirth, or what. I don't want to know. The shoes, they went into the garbage when I got home. At least Chucks are pretty cheap. And the shot girls. Whew. I know these girls are just doing their jobs, but don't even acknowledge them. Look away. Pretend you're deaf. Stop, drop, and roll. Play dead. Anything. The merest nod or shake of your head, the tiniest parting of your lips, will be construed as "Yes, I would like five of those beaker things full of Liquid Plumber please!" To make matters worse, they'll try to make you drink the shot out of their mouths, some Mama-bird to baby-bird type of move. I hate to sound like, I don't know, Wilfred Brimley, but no thanks. I enjoy my Herpes-free life. If that's your thing, though---as it seemed to be for a few older guys in Hawaiian shirts dancing as if trying to put out flames---then this might be your mecca. In the beginning of my pregnancy, there were concerns due to some bleeding. Because of these concerns and this being my first pregnancy, I was obviously nervous. One of the doctors there ordered several tests to be done at a local Quest Diagnostics and reported that test results would be back to me within 24-48 hours. After each of the 3 tests, I called after 48 hours to get my results and each time, the receptionist took my name, informed me that no one was currently on staff to get my results to me, and told me to wait. After the third time of this happening and receiving my results late, I drove to the office to ask the receptionist if she could get someone to print out my results. When I walked in, she looked at me, heard the phone ring, and answered it..which I understand. However, she never asked the person to hold or motioned to me that it would be a minute. She let me stand there and then carried on a personal conversation with a doctor that works there. "Oh, hi Thomas!! My family? They're good. Great Mother's Day. How was yours?" This went on for about 3-5 minutes and when she was done with her small talk, she transfered him to his co-worker. She then looked up at me like I was a nuisance and said, "can I help you?" I told her why I was there and she then disappeared for 10-15 minutes with no warning of where she was going or when she would be back. She reappeared to tell me it would be a little while. I said, "well can you give me an idea of how long because I have to go back to work?" She snapped back dryly, "have a seat." A lab tech then appeared and gave me my results with no explanation of what they meant, although I knew they weren't good from doing some research myself. I started crying a little out of confusion over the bad results and feeling like I had been mistreated by the staff and the lab tech just stood there. The receptioist then appeared and said, "if you're going to get this upset, you'll have to go into an office." No one once asked if I was okay or offered any support over these results. I was then ushered into Dr. Lisa Leone's office, someone who had obviously already been briefed by the awful receptionist, who treated me like I was also a nuisance. She proceeded to tell me that I should know that they "don't ignore their clients there" and I should stop calling for results because they would get to me when they had something to report. She also went on to say "you're hardly even pregnant, so there's really not much we can tell you." She never asked if I was okay. She actually made me feel worse. Just because I was in the first 1-2 months of pregnancy, does that mean my feelings over bad test results should not count as much or that I should not get as much support or consultation? I left without any rebuttal or any more discussion because I felt I had been totally mistreated and I had already decided I would switch doctors. The only highlight of my experience here was a follow-up phone call from a nurse practitioner, Kristin, who had called to make sure I understood the results the lab tech had given me. I have since switched to Penn Medicine at Radnor and have had a much more professional and supportive experience.

I then explained to her that I'd requested additional tortillas to finish my meal with, now, 20 minutes ago and never received them, nor had I even seen our waiter until just then. Instead of trying to make it right in any way, I was informed that the fajitas come with three tortillas, and additional would cost extra. Throughout this encounter she and the waiter kept repeating that the entree came with only 3 tortillas, and that it was my fault for not finishing my meal. I gave up, and paid the bill, which I'll be disputing with the bank shortly after wrapping up this review The short, tl;dr version: I had a complaint, and they did not seem to care, nor was there anyone with any authority to make anything right. text: I've been to Dickie Brennan's Steak House nearly a dozen times over the past ten years, and while I once thought it to be a very respectable steak house, my most recent experiences have not met expectations. Deciding to head out to Dickie's with a friend of mine before an evening of revelry on Bourbon Street, I warned him beforehand that there are better steak houses in New Orleans, but I reasoned that this was going to get us to our real nightly mission fastest due to its fantastic location. As I ordered myself a scotch, one thing off the bat that I noticed on this visit is that Dickie Brennan's is comparatively expensive in a city with so many great steak options. A shot of plain 'ol 16-year Lagavulin cost me $21, which I've not paid in the U.S. outside of Manhattan or Beverly Hills. I asked for still water with my meal, and was presented with a bottle of Mountain Valley Spring Water ($3) "which is from Arkansas," explained my waiter, who presented it to me like it was a bottle of 1945 Mouton. I laughed audibly, as it reminded me of a scene from the Penn & Teller TV show where they were filling water bottles with garden hoses and convincing people they were being served premium water. I somehow remember the seafood gumbo ($7) being better at Dickie Brennan's. Containing chunks of andouille sausage, their gumbo is a bit of an oddity in New Orleans, with many restaurants preferring to use only shellfish in their seafood gumbos. Dickie Brennan's gumbo is not a particularly dark gumbo (despite their claims to the contrary), nor did it taste bad, but I could not find any seafood in it other than shrimp, despite it being billed as having P&J oysters and "seasonal fish." I split the Barbecue Shrimp & Grits appetizer ($10.50) with my friend. They can offer this "Mr. B's-style" with heads-on, or peeled and de-headed. We opted for the latter, as we refused to wear a bib for an appetizer. The shrimp and sauce were good - the shrimp were served in a typical butter and Worcestershire-based sauce, not the type of barbecue sauce you'd find outside of New Orleans. The Jalapeño Cheddar Grit cake that comes with this appetizer tasted blander than it sounded. For my steak, I ordered the 24 ounce Bone-In "Cowboy" Rib Eye daily special ($42). It's a steak - it's hard to screw up a USDA prime rib eye done to someone's preference. I personally like my steak with a bit more of a crust (especially at medium-rare), but it was good nonetheless. The Pepper-Cream Bourbon sauce, on the other hand, is garbage. I'm glad I only dabbed a little bit on some of my steak, as it would have ruined my meal. It's not an ill-conceived idea, but the execution is horrible. Not knowing whether it wants to be sweet or savory, it is a virtually inedible abomination. My friend and I split a side of Potatoes Au Gratin ($6.50) which was underwhelming and undercooked. Service was solid, as always. Overall atmosphere and lighting is great if you like steak houses. The dining room is filled with lots of ancient sugar daddy types with beautiful young women in fancy dresses. It's a nice place to dine. The food, unfortunately, does not always deliver for the price. Dickie Brennan's is an alright steakhouse - but its inconsistency is maddening and I'm afraid there are too many other great dining options to keep it in my rotation of restaurants I will visit upon future trips to New Orleans.
label: NEG

text: Lovely lunch today. I couldn't stop ordering. Next, a thigh of crispy-brown, juicy chicken (still warm) that was beautifully cooked (no red stuff near the bone, not overcooked dry) and tasted delicious. I "tasted" the mashed potatoes, which are clearly fake. I hate that, although I'm quite surprised they really didn't taste that bad, so maybe they're doctored in some way. I tasted one liver, because I just couldn't resist, even though I was stuffed. It was divine. A little limp (from steaming in the box), but the breading flavor was good, and the liver wasn't over-cooked. There's a boat-load of chicken livers -- the 8x8x3-inch box was stuffed to the top! Considering the lunch damage, I've still got a massive bunch of livers, four pieces of chicken and a serving of mashed potatoes. How many meals is that? The whole shebang cost $14.07. Inside Porter's there's an ample ordering area. Eating space is four tables of four chairs, and four round elevated bar tables of two chairs. I don't think I'd consider eating in, but I'll surely get carryouts again! Thanks, Yelp! and Yelpers, for steering me to Porter's!! It's a find!

text: I went to the newest location of Good Earth Cafe with my sister, Michelle, for lunch. We ended up splitting their macaroni and cheese and a vegetarian breakfast panini. They both tasted awesome! The macaroni tasted like homemade macaroni and it was very tasty! Still, there was a pesto sauce that made the sandwich so flavorful and scrumptious. The service was excellent! We weren't sure what type of drink to get. We just knew we wanted something slushy to enjoy in the sun. The girl behind the counter gave us a bunch of suggestions and we loved our drinks! I got the mocha frappe (yum!) and Michelle ordered the banana cafe frappe (double yum!). The drinks were frothy and not too sweet. The price was alright. It came to about $20 for two frappes, macaroni, and a breakfast panini. Walking into the restaurant, there was so much space! Lots of tables to sit at and huge counter space to look at the large variety of foods. The whole shop had a really nice, friendly atmosphere. Not like some coffee shops where everyone seems quite pretentious. We were hoping to enjoy some of the sun and were lucky enough to get a spot on their patio. With the sun shining and our delicious treats, it was a fabulous lunch experience! I already want to go back again and enjoy another meal on their patio. text: The essence of local. You get a choice from a few main dishes and two sides. The menu is limited but what they offer has excellent flavor right up there with the big name restaurants but at a fraction of the price. We had the fried fish which was catfish that day and crawfish étouffée. We tried all four side dishes, potato salad, peas, green salad and Mac & cheese. My wife lived in New Orleans for ten years and the catfish was as good as it gets, crispy and moist and the tartar sauce was some of the best she's ever had. The crawfish étouffée was outstanding, tender and nicely spiced. All the sides were good but the potato salad was great with lots of chopped hard boiled eggs and celery and the Mac & cheese was nice and cheesy and not gritty. Oh, did I mention the fresh home made cookies? We had two peanut butter cookies that were moist and really pea nutty. Way too much food to eat and our total with drinks was $17 for two. Don't expect white table cloths and linen napkins. The atmosphere is paper plates and plastic forks and drink out of the bottle. There are only five tables and most folks do take out. This is a down to earth real New Orleans neighborhood place to relax with really friendly locals and enjoy some great food at an incredibly good price, and it's air conditioned.

Maybe it was because I picked it up around 7 PM, but the cake was pretty dry. (Perhaps that's why most other cupcake shops around the city don't stay open so late?) The first bite was tasty and chocolate, but very dry. The other thing that hit me was the sugar overload. I like sweet things, but the sweetness of this cake was way too intense for my tastes. It took me a while to find the "cheesecake filling in the centre." When I found it, I was able to chow down on it in just one bite. I'm sure on its own, it would have been tasty, but it had so little sugar in it that it tasted almost bitter in comparison to the rest of the cake. If it was a bit sweeter, and the cake a little less so, they might have been a nice contrast to each other, but this was just gross. The cream cheese icing was good, but nothing worth writing home about. I finished the icing, but threw away the rest of the cake. At $4 a pop, this baby didn't come cheap, either. Bummer. text: Tragedy! I'm starting to feel evil for the less-than-stellar reviews I've been positing. I sincerely do not go out of my way to be vindictive and will make a real effort in the future to call out the good experiences I've had instead of focusing on the negative. This, however, will not be one such. We've given this place 3 very sincere chances. It's local to where we live so it would make all the sense in the world that we'd want it to work for us. Additionally, it tends to look like it's doing a thriving business so we kept checking ourselves thinking we had an anomaly experience and it really was good. But tonight was strike three and we definitely won't be going back. There was no singular thing that I can pin my gripe on -- just a whole lot of little things that add up to a literal bad taste in one's mouth. But highlights: Warm caesar salad with wilted greens and flacid crutons clearly made at least several hours in advance (even though the restaurant was not so busy that they would need to do this.) A "martini" list that had every friggin' type of flavored VODKA but not a single gin. A general note: a martini is -- by strictest definition in the goddam dictionary -- gin and dry vermouth. If contemporary trend has raped it of this title and wants to classify anything dumped into a martini glass as a martini, then have at. But *PLEASE* respect your elders and include the gin martini on the list. Chicken saltimbocca that somehow managed to be both bland and salty at the same time (served, incidentally, with a veggie medley that looked like it had been imported special from the Bob Evans "oriental stir fry" menu. One of the highlights at Cutillo's might be the dinner rolls they put out but -- even at the height of the dinner hour -- I was advised that they were done with em' for the night because there weren't many people eating. All of this might be understandable or even excusable, except that the night before I was eating at a GOOD Italian joint called Nizza in Hell's Kitchen, NYC, and was able to walk away having had an infinitely better meal and paid less for it (look for the Nizza review next -- it'll prove that I'm capable of being complimentary.) I should mention the bar might be one of the saving graces, with a clearly dedicated and insular group of regulars clinging to the periphery like it was an overturned life raft. I *think* the manager was among them -- or at least it was someone who looked more officious than the rest. But the 15 foot trek to our table to check on us was evidently beyond the call of duty and she contented herself with the occasional indifferent glance. I think that's about all I can say. For the price, one is better off going elsewhere and unfortunately one feels that even Olive Garden might be a better bet. Oh - I don't think it's exactly a coincidence that this will be only the second Yelp review posted; one has the distinct feeling that the restaurant -- its decor, the menu and many of the regulars -- ceased evolving around the time of the Commodore 64. This place CAN boast beautiful tree-lined views of a river, with natural atrium lighting and skylights, but the pine plank woodwork, pleather bar chairs and canopy of spider plants makes it look like a hang out that would make Jack, Janet and Chrissy from Three's Company proud.

text: Jones, you were one of the first places I ever visited when I moved to Philadelphia. You were the last place I visited before I left. The menu reminded me of everything I wished my health food-loving mom would have made when I was a kid. My boyfriend had the Chicken and Waffles, which were as good as the ones in South Central. He had a side of the slimmest, saltiest French fries ever, which were amazing to dip into the homemade chicken gravy. I was a little more restrained with the Sesame Seared Tuna. The tuna was just the right shade of rare with a tangy wasabi-soy sauce to compliment it. The best part of our first visit were the drinks. It didn't matter which drink we had--be it one of the hand-stirred fruity cocktails or the sparkling Jones soda--everything was good. Our server was attentive and wonderful and introduced me to the Poached Pear Martini, which is still one of my favourite drinks anywhere. Every other visit has promised the same, whether we've crawled in there late night after hitting the city or stumbled in on a Sunday morning for a hangover cure. We both have our favourites, but I'll sometimes get a wild craving for the French fries and chicken gravy and we know where to go. Their Potato Pancakes are to die for, as is the Baked Macaroni and Cheese. It's all the type of food that your grandma might make you if you visited on a Saturday afternoon, and that's okay. text: My husband and I are from Austin, so we really love Texas BBQ. We're not really experts in pulled pork or deep south BBQ. We were really intrigued when we found this place, which is only a minute away from where we live. We shared their 2 meat combo platter and got the baby back ribs and the sliced brisket with the carolina sauce, plus the sweet potato fries and cole slaw, which came out to a little under $15. The store layout is similar to a local pizza joint-- not a good place to eat in IMO (although there are tables and chairs) but great for takeout. I read an article they had hanging on their wall about the restaurant, and it said that Fletcher's was a restaurant that featured a sampling of all different types of BBQ- brisket from Texas, plus ribs and pulled pork from other parts of the south. They also have several types of sauce-- again, one Texas-inspired, another carolina, and a third that I don't remember. It's family-run by a family that decided to pursue their dreams away from corporate America. I'm always excited to try out local businesses. They said that they had been open for about 2 years. Being from Texas, I had a few expectations of what a BBQ place should be like, but it could just be that people do BBQ differently in different places. The menu features chopped and sliced brisket, ribs, pulled pork and pulled chicken, plus a few other things like a smoked whole or half chicken. Interestingly, they don't have any sausage, which to me should be a staple. Their sides are also a mix of different places-- cole slaw, sweet potato fries, collard greens, tater tots, mac and cheese, and baked beans.... but no potato salad, which again is a staple down in Texas. The thing that bugged me the most was that there was no sweet tea to be found, but I'd rather take a place with no sweet tea and great BBQ than a place with bad BBQ and great sweet tea. No free side items like pickles or onions were available either. The brisket was sliced generously, and not thinly. it's wasn't melt-in-your-mouth but it wasn't super chewy either. My favorite part was that it wasn't too charred on the outside but had nice darkness to it. The baby back ribs are fall-off-the-bone. I can see why the ribs got rave reviews from other yelpers. I wish there was more sauce on the meat, but that's probably a personal preference, as I'm used to there being extra tubs of sauce to dunk your meat in as opposed to the sauce only being poured directly onto the meat. I really liked that the meat was served on top of a delicious buttered piece of Texas toast. Delicious! I'm so glad to find a place that does BBQ well right here in Abington and that I don't need to drive 1600 miles to get it. It's not pure Texas BBQ but both my husband and I really enjoyed our meal. We'll be back, and next time we'll try the pulled pork and some different sides!

text: My wife and I went on a tapa style restaurant crawl over the weekend starting at Barbuzzo (which was as delicious as ever). Towards the end of our meal we asked our bartender about any good restaurant recs in the area, and he mentioned that The Oyster House on Sansom had just undergone some sort of renovation/change in ownership and it was GOOD. (Not sure how long ago this happened, but I vaguely remember reading a review in the Inquirer a while back). Anyway, being a beautiful June evening we wandered the few blocks down Sansom, and walked into the Oyster House. The place was hopping, and just before we sat down I noticed the specials board stated that they were running $1 Happy Hour oysters from 9-11 pm on Saturday. It was Saturday, and about 7:30pm, so being the cheap bastard that I am, we left and carried on down the street to Tinto (review soon to come), and The Dandelion Pub (battle rap style review soon to come). Upon our return, the place was jammed. Not a seat was to be had at the enormous bar that snakes it's way through the whole restaurant. The place was crowded with a mix of couples out on the town (like us), tables of friends, and a smattering of hipsters. Nobody was overly dressed, and very few people looked like they had just rolled out of bed. The two lovely hostesses promptly took my name, told us to grab a drink if we wanted, and that they would find us as soon as two seats opened up. Once at the bar, I had to inquire about the champagne special. Apparently, it comes in a can. I declined, and ordered a $3 Preininger, I mean Kenzinger, and my wife had a glass of house white. Both of us approved of our drinks. I had never had Kenzinger before, and found it a crisp refreshing pilsner perfectly suited for the weather, and some oysters. Speaking of oysters, the bartender told us that the $1 Happy Hour special only refers to the oyster of the day, which was a Delaware Bay oyster, not a choice of any of the 6 other oysters they offer. Being unsure of whether I have ever tried a Delaware Bay oyster, I was almost as apprehensive about the prospect of eating something out of the scummy Delaware Bay as I was about the champagne in a can. After quickly being seated at the bar, my wife and I both agreed that we'd be brave, and order just 6 of them in case they were repulsive. Thankfully, they were not, and we quickly ordered six more. The oysters were medium in size, had very low salinity, and were extremely creamy in the mouth. I liked them. Can't believe I just wrote the line, creamy in the mouth, but dammit they were. My only gripe was that the oysters were not fully shucked, and were still attached to the shell. Also, there was absolutely no oyster liquor in the shell. Not sure if it that is due to the kind of oyster, but I like the juice. Being the last stop on the tapa crawl, we decided to call it a night, but vowed we'd return for more. Apparently, they offer something called "Tuesday Night Dump Dinner". As unappetizing as it sounds, it looks like a Pile O' Seafood. I am good with that. And for 19 bucks, I am good with that, too. I definitely, enjoyed our brief snack, and was impressed with the fantastic service from both hostesses, and bartenders. The bartenders were swamped, but they handled it with ease, and personable service. Also, loved the seafood house decor with a myriad of oyster plates decorating the walls. We are both excited to return, and will hopefully make it back for Dump Night.

text: Were in town visiting my folks S. of Tucson and decided we'd like to go for something at least nice before the night was out on New Year's Eve and decided on this place after looking at our options on Restaurants.com where at least we could get a price break. The menu sounded promising and lately mid to high end hotels have been doing a better job of having a quality restaurant experience. Well, this place is trying hard but just can't pull it off. First, the location inside the Sheraton is strange-it is buried in the middle-past a bunch of rooms and past the pool. Once inside, the decor was nice but somehow it didn't have a lively atmosphere. Maybe that is because it was about a third full on New Year's Eve at 9 pm. I am more used to good hotel restaurants being near the entrance of the hotel where you really don't even have to go into the hotel and thus end up feeling autonomous. The service was middling. Our waitress seemed tentative and unsure. The broth for the tortilla soup was quite lukewarm-and having her serve it at the table allowed her the opportunity to spill some of it all around the outside of the bowl. Our entrees (Carne Asada and one of the steak options which no longer seems to be on their website menu) were fine but nothing that made you savor it for long. The worst part was waiting over 20 minutes for our tiramisu and creme brule at around 10:30 when I think there was only one other table in the place and they were working on their appetizers. I'm guessing that the chef was also pulling dessert duty. In closing, this place looks fine, has a nice sounding menu with a potentially innovative approach but manages to fall short what a really good restaurant should be even in a hotel environment.

text: Dear people of Chinatown (and those who venture into it), Mandarin and Szechuan does not mean Taiwanese. I'm not even sure if the staff here is Taiwanese. I had asked them if they had "Dan Bing" and they looked at me like I wanted an enchilada. Back me up here, my fellow Taiwanese! But, they do have some dishes from Taiwan on the menu. With that settled, let's get to the good (and bad) stuff. Definitely Order: + Peking Noodle (Ja Jiang Mien) - This is the reason I love coming here. This is the Chinese version of Spaghetti alla Bolognese. Salty, sweet, spicy, crunchy bean sauce over thick Chinese noodles. The noodles are on the softer side (old school Asians don't believe in al dente) and mix very well with the sauce. + Scallion Pancake - The best scallion pancake in the city. It's not thick like other places, and it's thin enough where it's not a cracker, either. The best part is the dipping sauce. Instead of the standard black vinegar mixture, the sauce is clear! I think it tastes better than its dark counterpart. + Ma Po Tofu - I love ma po tofu. When I can't have my mom's, I come here for it. Maybe Order: + Taiwan Beef Noodle Soup - The noodle soup tastes pretty authentic, although it is on the blander side. + Pai Goo Fan - Fried pork chops w/ pickled veggies over rice. I like this one, but the pork chops need to be crispier. Don't Order: + Soup Dumplings - Tastes like the frozen kind. There are other spots in town if you're craving these little exploding dumpling balls. + Chinese-American Dishes - General Tso's chicken, beef and broccoli, orange chicken, and shrimp in lobster sauce? Umm... no. I just noticed that all of the dishes listed under "Maybe" are the Taiwanese dishes, weird. The service, food, and prices at Empress Garden are great. Now if I can only find a place that makes Dan Bing....
label: POS

text: The Bella Boutique looks like an amazing place to get 2nd hand vintage and contemporary designer clothing and accessories for a decent price BUT DO NOT BE FOOLED!!! Don't get me wrong I've purchased a cool vintage belt and a couple pairs of shoes there before BUT YOU HAVE TO BE VERY CAREFUL!! I've never check for the authenticity of my shoes but I wouldn't be surprised if they were FAKE. I bought a Gucci bag from them this past summer and everything SEEMED legit. The bag smelled like leather, came with a Gucci dust bag and the little Gucci booklet. They have section full of bags and clothing that are clearly knock-offs so you would assume that everything behind the counter was the real stuff!....I was somewhat in a rush and trusted that I would not be sold anything fake without my knowledge! This store is in a decent area and seems to be a credible place, how silly to assume! When I purchased the bag for $300 I had to sign a waiver basically saying that if the bag was fake they were not liable which didn't make much sense to me because they are running a consignment shop with a lot of designer pieces therefore someone should be trained to authenticate merchandise if you are passing it off as authentic designer merchandise!!!! NOT TO MENTION THE FACT THAT IT IS ILLEGAL TO SELL MERCHANDISE UNDER A DESIGNER NAME IF IT IS NOT!!! I was excited that I snagged this bag for such a good price but upon further inspection their were a few things that made me suspicious about the bag. One thing I can say is that the way merchandise is produced today is no match to the quality of the previous decades, designer or not but it still was enough to make me question it. After thorough investigating on the internet i discovered the bag was FAKE! FAKE! FAKE!!!!! I was soooo upset I wanted to make my claim and return the bag and even report the store but I remembered that I foolishly signed the waiver so there was really nothing I could do. This was definitely one of the best knock-offs I've ever seen, very convincing! Which leads me to believe this is an inside job especially after reading other reviews and seeing that other people have had the same experience. I wouldn't be surprised if the owner has fake stuff being shipped to the store. Unfortunately I will have to take my $300 as a lesson learned and to top it off their customer service sucks!! You will only be greeted and treated nicely if they think you're going to spend money!! This is definitely not an establishment I want to support with my money! They're running a real scandal over there and need to be shut down.

text: I have a long review written but here is the short version: Food: 2 out of 5 stars- well conceived but poorly executed dishes. HUGE portions, which in my opinion is a sign of subpar food. Fish was overdone and definitely was frozen, not fresh. Tables are extremely cramped Long version: My girlfriend and I both love to try new places to explore great food. We decided to look on yelp and we both were in the mood for Mexican which led us to Cantina Dos Segundos. After careful reading of reviews and perusing the menu we decided to give it a go. We arrived at 5pm to a completely empty restaurant and immediately felt slightly awkward because the entire wait staff seemed annoyed we had to break up their powwow. Thus started and evening of sincere disappointment. The tables meant for 2 are completely too small- after our drinks, chips and salsa, and appetizer were all on the table- there was literally no room. So much so, our server stacked our chip bowl between the two salsa bowls. Every maneuver had to be carefully thought out as not to spill something. I'm not sure if we caught the kitchen on an off day or perhaps an off hour. We started with the Costillitas for an appetizer. The ribs were old and dried out. I suspected that had been cooked previously in the day if not on an earlier day and been reheated. The sauce was very very thickened and dried to the plate (as if sat under a heat lamp or nuked in the microwave). Even the salsa had evidence of sitting out to dry. Then entrees- I ordered the Tinga Poblana de Cerdo, which is essentially a pork shoulder, chorizo, and potato stew. Again it definitely was evident that the order had been microwaved (Plate was too hot to touch, stew was MOLTEN hot and a slight crust had formed around the top rim). I can expect, even hope, a stew to be prepared in advance and left cooking all day (mmmm ) but it was my suspicion it had been prepared another day, refrigerated, then reheated for me. My girlfriend ordered the Mahi Mahi. It was quite fishy and probably one of the driest pieces of fish i've ever eaten. Both entrees also came with a massive amount of throw-away sides like reheated rice and veggies. In my mind- it seemed like we came at an off hour. I am going to give them the benefit of the doubt and say MAYBE they cook to order during normal dinner hours and perhaps we came too early that we caught them at a bad time. One thing is for sure. I know when my order is made-to-order and when it has been reheated. i can say for 90% certainty that every single thing i consumed that day had been cooked on a previous date and my chef for the day was a commercial microwave. I would consider giving them another chance to taste some of these dishes when they are fresh, but unfortunately, with so many great choices in philly for good food, i can say I wont be back by my own choosing.
label: NEG

text: Listen, if you work in Manayunk, live in Manayunk, or plan on passing through it- you MUST get a sandwich at Angelo and Josephine's. Much of the long sandwich list are combinations of Italian deli meats and accompaniments. If none of the pre-set combos strike your fancy, you can easily create your own or make substitutes. The ingredients are all high high quality. You will find no slimy deli meat here. The sandwiches are piled with the cured meat slices; they are quite big. Plus- how can you not be completely in love with a sandwich joint that puts an extra layer of meat on TOP of the sandwich. Completely unnecessary, completely awesome. My sandwich was hot sorpressata, hot cappicolla, provolone, and tomato. Sandwiches run around 6 or $7. If I see homemade roast pork on a menu there is a 100% guarantee that I will order it. I was told that Grandma makes it fresh here every morning from an old family recipe. The juicy slices were exactly what I was hoping for. This pork makes you stop and take notice. It was somehow light but also full of flavor. I wouldn't be surprised if Grandma had a conversation with the pig and asked him what seasonings would be ideal to bring out his maximum delicious potential. Garlic was definitely mentioned in that conversation. The pork is so good that it barely needs anything with it, but sharp provolone is the appropriate dairy addition. I liked both sandwiches so much, and would advise coming with a friend so you can go halvsies with one stacked deli sandwich and one roast pork sandwich. Angelo and Josephine's sandwiches are the kind of secret I want to shout about from the rooftops.

Just be careful that you don't valet, it's costly and not worth it. Parking is plentiful and easy. text: I am never amazed when people rate the exact opposite as I do or have completely different experiences as I. Usually though, I am the one being a hard-ass about a place. This time is different. I had to check the address to make sure this was the same restaurant other people had reviewed. We had gone to the Middle-Eastern market in this building before and we saw that this restaurant had opened. But living on the Mainland (East Bank) we would just go to Pyramids or Mona's. So it never was an issue. Today, however, while making one of the many, many, many trips for supplies that all new home owners make, we got the hungers something fierce. As usual, I wanted Asian (Thai, Vietnamese, even Chinese). The girly, as always, wanted Mexican. As we drove, I just mentioned Middle Eastern and just to keep either of us from getting what we wanted, she said to go there. As we walked in, the guy behind the counter opened the door for us and let is sit where we wanted. We were the only native English speakers in the restaurant. Good sign. That changed as it got closer to normal dinner hour, but still, a good sign for us. We looked over the menu and I have to admit, the prices were really quite good. I'm surprised this place as a $$ rating. At first I wanted a gyro and she wanted the catfish done in their special style but after looking at all the appetizers, we settled for getting a chicken Shawarma (Girly likes them, I usually think they are dry like sponge) and the appetizer sampler. A Lebanese tea for the Girly (She describes it as "Drinking Sunshine in a Rose Garden....I know..she's a cheesy-girly). I had the Guava drink (Sweet but darn did it go well with the foods). The drinks came first, followed by the bread and two little plates, then 2 more little plates, then a big platter. The little plates were: hummus (really creamy and nicely balanced) labna (creamy but not my style. Girly adored it), baba ganouj (Creamy, smoky, lemony...I don't usually like it. I did this time), and Turkish "salad" (A tomato based sauce that I actually really liked...and I don't like tomato sauces). On the big platter was: the veg-head stuffed grape leaves( The girly liked them a lot) Fatouche (Super fresh, a little lemony) Falafel (Ok...big time hard to admit...they were the best I've ever had...EVER. This city or any other I've lived in, home made or otherwise. Sorry Pyramids, can we still be friends?) Now for the sammach. The chicken Shawarma, as I mentioned, is usually not something I like. Most seem to be nuked and dried. This had that moist and rich flavor like really well marinated Mexican chicken. Not anything you can get out of a box, this was slow marinated and amazing. I actually wanted to order another Shawarma for desert. I will even forgive the guy for cutting it so the Girly got more than half...One day... Now, this entire feast cost about 24 bucks. Side notes. As you may know if you read my reviews, I'm an ass about CLEAN places. This place was clean, simply decorated, but clean. Good Service, extremely friendly and helpful staff and good value for cheap-asses like us. We WILL go back and expect anyone who like Middle Eastern to get your booties over there. I will reserve that 5th star for our 3rd trip there since almost no restaurant seems to be able to keep up the quality for 3 visits.

text: We were anxious to try The Flaming Torch since it is on many people's most romantic in New Orleans list. Although it did satisfy several of the "romantic requirements" by being dimly lit, quaint, and quiet the experience was overall underwhelming. We were saddened to learn we would be unable to dine outdoors due to the fact their outdoor furnishings were in disrepair. Not a huge issue, but disappointing none the less. Now the saddest part, the quantity and quality of the meal. We were aware this was a French restaurant so expected smaller portions. I did however, expect more than 5 green beans (or as the waiter corrected us on multiple occasions Haricot Vert) and 2 fingerling potatoes. Maybe it's just me, but if I drop 38 bucks on an entree I expect a fair amount of groceries (now I sound like a hillbilly but you get the point.) Sadly, even the morsels of food provided were inedible. There was large chunks of sea salt covering EVERYTHING! So much so, that the waiter was able to spot the salt from his standing position and agreed to take it back to the kitchen. The reason that they did get the 2 stars I awarded was the fact they did attempt to satisfy us by making new entrees and preparing a to-go bag for us as we had after dinner plans. However there were no special accommodations made on the final bill, but to be fair, I didn't press the issue. I simply wanted to pay the over 100 dollar dinner-for-two tab and quickly forget our evening at The Flaming Torch.
label: NEG

text: I am usually not a person to go into a pet store as I am very pro adoption and believe that anything you can get at stores like this you can buy at a pet supply store. About a week ago I had to grab some live meal worms for my turtle because he went off his food and I knew he could not refuse those. I waited 30 minutes before someone finally helped me. During that time I asked several people for help and they said that the area I wanted help in was not their area. After I got help (finally) I went over to the small live pet area and I noticed several were sick with a fungal infection of some kind. I know this because I do a lot of rescue work and see it a lot. I told the girl cleaning cages and she stated that they were fine and that she just checked on them. When I pointed out that Ring worm could be the cause and that she should go to her Dr. to get checked she freaked out, grabbed the sick baby guinea pig and a baby bunny and took them into the back. I would NEVER suggest this store. They will sell you sick, pregnant, and un handled pets.

I had hoped to just have them tack on a cheap one and get away with less than $150. Mufflers and labour ain't cheap. The day I went, the place was quite busy. They graciously agreed to look at it right away, and even allowed me to scamper down into the pit to have a look at the underside of my new ride. Sure enough, no muffler. And worse, the exhaust pipe from headers to where the muffler ought to be was a rust eaten mess. The guy helping me (I have misplaced his name, tho I am sure he still has it well secured) was able to find a generic muffler for $40, and then advised me about my choices to have them make a new pipe for $160, or have them order one in for $140. I figured it was gonna cost me at least $300 with labour on top of that, but the price came out to $200! That is a phenomenal price for entire exhaust pipe AND muffler AND labour! They did the repairs while I was at work, and I took a cab back to pick my car up after hours. They had no problem leaving the keys in it, the paperwork on my seat, as I had paid beforehand. No upsell, just the facts and choices, and they treated me like I had a brain in my head, and not just some useless girl. Major points in my books.

text: Unfortunately a friend was not available when I arrived to Philadelphia tired and worn so I thought need a hotel and had stayed here before. The hotel location and amenities are good. Penn graduate school alumni here and proud to call Philadelphia PA my home town, but my goodness what happened to good ole customer service and taking the time to explain things to folks. The situation was that my blow dryer wouldn't work. I call the front desk and asked for a replacement to be sent to my room. Shortly a knock comes to the door. I answer handing what I thought was a broken blow dryer to the male housekeeping person. He proceeds to try to walk into my room. I stand in front of him offering what I thought was a broken blow dryer. He asserts with body language that he is coming into my room. I say what are you doing I just want a blow dryer. He finally explains after demonstrating annoyance (facial distortion and tonal voice quality) with my blocking his entrance into the room I paid to use, that I may have tricked the switch on the plug and caused the blow dryer not to work. As it happens I had just tried to use the blow dryer but it would not turn on. Any way he comes into the room pushes some buttons on the plug and the thing works. I did not feel comfortable with the exchange so I call downstairs and ask for management. Someone by the name of Josh says I am one of the managers. I explain my difficulty with the demeanor of the person that came to the door and that I had no idea prior to him coming that he would need to enter my room. I explained that the party and the person who sent him needed to understanding the potential dynamics and concerns of a male entering the room of a customer who happened to be a female in her room alone. The party says the insincere apologetic words from his mouth but not until after he tells that he is going to speak with party right now who is standing in his location. He returns to the phone and proceeds to defend the party with no apparent empathy for my perspective and position as a female. In closing, do know that if you ask for a blow dryer because for whatever reason yours is not working they are not bringing a new one to you but thinking that they should come into your room and fix it without explaining that to you in advance. Common courtesy is minimized and job efficacy and timeliness are maximized! But what a dissappointment--just a explaination and some empathy would have gone a long way. Next time I believe I will spend my money elsewhere, in hopes of having a more pleasant experience. It is easy to smile and be nice to people when everything is going well. text: Came in here late night on a Saturday after being told London Grill had closed their kitchen early. So the bartender suggested we check out Lemon Hill instead. We ordered dirty rice balls for an appetizer and got some patty melts for the main course. We had been craving the London burger at LG so we figured this would come close. Boy, were we wrong! The dirty rice balls came out - they look like hush puppies kind of, deep fried exterior with a dipping sauce on the side. Took a bite - they were ice cold in the middle. Not sure how they make these in advance for prep (freeze them in advance, fridge them to stay firm before frying), but you could at least check the internal temp of the food you're sending out of the kitchen. It was a major turn off. Not the kind of first impression you want to leave with customers, esp. considering the place is so new & has a reputation to uphold based on the fact that it's joint venture between 2 well regarded city establishments: Supper & Franklin Mortgage. Patty melts came out shortly after. Menu said they came with waffle fries - they were more like fried potato slices with crinkles on them; looked and tasted like they came out of a bag. Patty melt itself wasn't anything to write home about for what was probably like, $10-$12 (can't remember & can't look it up since Lemon Hill doesn't have their menu posted on their website. wtf?) Didn't try any drinks but some of the ones on the menu looked interesting. Guess you could always come here for cocktails instead of waiting on line at Franklin. I'd pass on the food though.

text: So Yang Ming was recently voted #1 in the Top 100 Overall Excellence category of Chinese restaurants in America by China Restaurant News. America's best Chinese restaurant, in other words. It's possible that Pot Stickers Asian Grill in Newark, Delaware is actually the 63rd best Asian restaurant in the US. But I doubt it. http://top100.chinesemenu.com/en/us/?type=winnerlist&a=overall-excellence&b=us&id=514825050 Fifteen of the restaurants on the list are buffets. C'mon. Buffets? I finally ate at Yang Ming tonight. The restaurant was packed for the Chinese New Year lion dance, but I only saw a handful of Asians-other than the staff. The food was American Chinese / "fusion". The dumplings we had were "house made", but with commercially-produced wrappers and the edges were dry. Maybe they sat too long before steaming. The entrees were heavy on the cornstarch sauces. There were few vegetable dishes on the menu. And no live seafood to choose from. How can this be considered the best--and from an Asian community authority? I have eaten exquisite Chinese food in San Francisco and New York. I find Yang Ming's status on this list disappointing if not downright embarrassing.

text: Don't go to Ablitt's cleaners! I brought a David Donahue shirt, with french cuffs, it was new and never worn, to Ablitt's to be cleaned and pressed and the shirt disappeared. The manager, Sean, said he has no idea what happened to my beautiful new shirt. Sean also said he didn't know about the incident, although an entry had been typed into my account on the company's computer. I was told about the comment, by the employee waiting on me, when I arrived to pick up my shirt. The employee was very courteous to me and respectful of the situation. The clerk said the comment stated that the shirt was sent out with another unknown customer. No one even apologized to me for the error, I mentioned this to Sean, the manager, who agreed that even he didn't apologize, very insensitive indeed! Sean, the manager, didn't know that I was a Senior Software Engineer, retired, specializing in databases, when he told me, over the phone, the data on the shirt didn't make it into the database. After I questioned him about Ablitt's lack of a system, with a unique identifier, to keep track of customers clothing, Sean said, "Ablitt's did in fact have a unique identifier," saying, "I'm looking at the information on the shirt at my computer right now," and relayed, correctly, all the information about my shirt to me, the pink stripes, the designers name, David Donahue, the date I brought it in to be cleaned, etc. if there was a unique identifier for each item of clothing at Ablitt's, each and every piece would be tracked and Ablitt's would have known what customer was given my shirt, as the clerk indicted, and called them to retrieve it. Also, if the data on my shirt wasn't in the database, as Sean indicated, he wouldn't have had access to it so someone entered the data into the database correctly. I asked Sean to pay me for the shirt and after telling me he wants my business, with small incentives offered, informed me I would have to wait 30 days for my money, he said this was company policy. Sean wants my business, he doesn't want to earn my business, if he did he would have been willing to negotiate the 30 day policy, after all Sean did say this was a rare event. I wonder, I can only trust that it is. The fact is, all policies are negotiable and not set in stone as Sean indicated and i was willing to wait a reasonable period of time. I fully understand it's a good idea to respect a company policy requiring a waiting period before receiving compensation for a lost item, just in case the item, in this case my shirt, is returned or discovered in the shop. I feel 30 days is unreasonable, in this case, since Ablitt's lost the shirt. Sean, to his credit, did promise to pay me 135.00 dollars for my shirt, in 30 days. Well, we'll see, I trust that he will. Mistakes happen in business, when they do it is a test of how a company will respond, revealing their level of commitment to customer service. Errors in business are an opportunity to increase clients trust and respect for that business, something Ablitt's failed to realize in my case. I will be updating this review on April 16th, the date I was told, by Sean the manager, I would receive my 135.00 dollars for the shirt that Ablitt's Cleaners lost. If I get the shirt returned sooner I will update this review then.

text: Yup, it is a bar But it's all mediocre So disappointed Like parents whose only child chooses to go to art school and study pottery, my disappointment in Ten Stone is both keen and lingering. I cringe when people say "I want to like this place, but..." then list all the reasons said place sucks. I don't want to be that guy, and I don't want to read that guy's reviews. However... I want to like Ten Stone. I can see the sign from my place. They have a respectable tap which changes on the regular. It's never crowded during the afternoons, so I come here occasionally with co-workers before late afternoon meetings. I don't go here in general though, because every time I do I'm reminded of my abject disappointment in the entire experience. First the positive. Their beer list is one of the best in the area, and they've always got a good diversity of stouts, lagers, IPA's and Ale's. They have a wide horseshoe shaped bar, and plenty of seating (albeit mostly 4-tops) during off-peak hours. Unlike other bars, it's pretty well lit. The orange walls and wood tables give the room a warm feel, and it's not terribly loud. There's some decent standing room around the bar itself, but nowhere to sit your drink while doing so. Despite all the seating in the main room, it seems like there is only ever one waiter on duty, so forget about getting any type of expedient service. Depending on the waiter, you might not even get a greeting. Hell depending on the time, you may not even get a beer, a clean table or a menu. It's a cycle; the service sucks because there's one miserable person on duty, and they're miserable because everyone thinks the service sucks. Note: hire more staff. But then there's the food. I've never eaten anything so absent of flavor. Everything from the hummus to the Cuban sandwich is completely unremarkable. When I'm eating there, my internal thought process is along the lines of "I'm eating this because my body needs nutrients to continue to function, not because it's any good." The meat is flavorless, as are most of the sauces. It's like it's been roasted/cooked with no regard to flavor or seasoning, only proper internal temperature. Everything I've eaten from here seems devoid of any type of seasoning, including salt. I was here on a Friday night recently, grabbed a beer at the crowded bar, and snagged a table. Cut to 30 minutes when the menu's finally arrived after flagging down the waitress and requesting them. Ten more minutes. The waitress came by for the food order, and I nearly had to grab her arm to alert her that we'd like another beer. Despite the empty glasses sitting on the table, she had no intention of asking if we'd like another round. We sat there for two hours and only had two beers (including the first one from the bar). I'd closed my bar tab already or I would have definitely just gone up and gotten it myself. When we finished the second beer, again with glasses empty on the table, she didn't ask if we wanted another round, she asked if we wanted the check. Kind of strange, no? I still tipped 20% because it's not her fault she's handling the entire floor, but damn was that the worst service I've ever gotten anywhere. So yeah, I really want to like Ten Stone. I can't even bring myself to give them one star despite all my annoyances and dislikes. If it were Tuesday night at 6PM and all I wanted was a beer or two, I'd head over and sit at the bar and likely have a decent experience. However I can still get a better experience at any number of places at the same time. It's a rare evening where I can be found at Ten Stone, one which won't be coming again anytime soon.

text: There are three things you should never hear a hairdresser say: "It'll look better when you get home." (it always looks better when you leave the shop, and that's not a way to handle someone's complaint that they don't like their cut.) "Play with it a few days and then you can call me." (It wasn't explained what would happen when I did call, which is that I didn't receive a call back.) "You can put product in it at home to make it look better." (Even though every cut I had in the past didn't require product to look good.) A haircut is something that can't or shouldn't be explained or excused. It is self-explanatory. You can't go to a party the next night and say: "My hair looks ridiculous, but I am playing with it." The cut is in the cut. Nothing else. One other thing that has been said about haircuts: Vidal Sasoon said if someone takes a razor to your hair, run! I should have. Why would you thin someone's hair who has naturally thick hair, especially when they've said the thing they want most out of the haircut is body and volume? Sergio was the one who cut my hair. He was very nice at the salon, and that might lead you, as it did me, to believe he knew what he was doing, or cared. But I had to live with it for weeks (and still am) after he cut it, no matter how nice he was for the hour I was there. When I commented that my hair on one side looked like it was bare, he said "I thought you were worried about your hair staying behind your ears." Yes, but I didn't want to look like a chunk had been taken out of my hair either. These things are not mutually exclusive. So he fixed that. What was this--Haircut by collaboration? Why would he let me, or anyone, for that matter, leave with hair that looks bad in any way? And make excuses about what was bad? When I went back to get a repair or ask for my money back, the shop was closed. (Thank God, because now I understand the insanity of trying to get a repair from the place that gave you a terrible cut in the first place). Another woman was there, too, and had a terrible story about a coloring that went badly wrong. People have gone to the salon in Lambertville--I believe Zanya--to get repairs from this shop, and I think that salon may have reason to open a special section of their shop to do this (perhaps they can hold group therapy sessions, as well.) It is really too bad. I tried a place on faith (and Yelp! reviews), and a great name, and the fact that it is a Paul Mitchell salon, and it failed, badly. I'm still waiting for it to grow out (another thing you shouldn't hear a hairdresser say, but that was said, as well.)

text: I was so excited to have a lunch date yesterday with one of my Yelp friends, Ms. Tracey W. When Yelpers get together, it is always so hard to pick a place to go. Being a gentleman, I told Tracey she could pick. She thought we should go some place new for both of us and doing that with two active Yelpers can be a challenge. After extensive debating, we selected The Fountain on Locust. I had been there once before, but was waiting for a second visit before reviewing and Tracey W. had it on her bucket list. TFL is a ice cream shop for adults. The menu of Martinis make me droll, I wanted a Dreamciscle Martini so bad, it just sounds luscious. Tracey W and I did have several good giggles. Starting off with our waiter having to come to our table multiple times just to get our order. Then posing our malt, shake and sandwiches for their closeups. I told Tracey on my first visit I had alcohol, but this time I wanted to experience a shake/malt. When you're at a soda fountain, you've got to experience a hand made shake and TFL does it oh so right. Every since I was a wee lad I have loved malt flavoring and the best malts are chocolate. Tracey went with a shake and choose chocolate too. I like the touch of bringing you the extra pour in the stainless mixing glass. Both of our drinks made that funny noise, when your straw has nothing else to pull up. That is a sign of a good drink, not bad manners. For lunch I had the Hot Roast Beef Melt and it was near orgasmic. I am a big beef eater and am partial to Angus Beef, which this is made from. Those big black cows, paid for my college education. This sandwich is savory Angus beef with white cheddar and grilled onion. It is served on a fresh baked baguette, that has Subway uttering, "how do they do that". It is also served with a house made horseradish sauce. I use to not be a fan of horseradish, but theirs has changed my mind and I'd buy in a jar if were available. (hint-hint) As a side I choose the Orange Onion Salad with Poppyseed Dressing. It is what the name says, oranges and red onion and nothing else. There is no lettuce in this salad. Once again, TFL impressed me with their house made dressing. It totally blew me away & I have family in the salad dressing business. Tracey's sandwich looked equally impressive. She was the perfect "girl" date ordering a Mixed Salad Sandwich. She was right in her review, saying the shake really didn't go with the food. However, we drank & ate what we wanted. Visualize a fresh baguette with melted Parmesan and Mozzarella Cheeses then stuffed with mixed lettuces, roasted red pepper, tomato, artichoke and a smear of house made pesto. You can make it St. Louis Style by adding meat (chicken), which Tracey did. I will order that sandwich on my next visit. I was tempted by her side salad which was the Stutz Salad, but I would have had to have them hold the walnuts. Not nuts about that nut. Otherwise, baby spinach, plump Mandarin oranges, goat cheese and a creamy marmalade dressing would be a perfect summer salad. Tracey W. mentioned our next outing we would drink and I must say that is great, but it also scares me. Without booze, we still managed to share family/life secrets. I'd be scared to see what we'd share if we had Vodka & beer in us. In closing if Tracey would have suggested ice cream for lunch, I would have called dibs on the Banana Split.

text: Hot Friday Night in Mid Summer w/ no idea what you would like to eat, but you would probably eat a burger. Head to Hickory Lane on the Corner of Corinthian and Fairmount. But before you head to this great BYOB, stop around the corner at the local Wine and Spirits store for a bottle of chilled white wine. This is how my night ended up about two Friday's ago with my girlfriend and I not knowing what to eat. Although I had heard the whispers of a new burger in the Fairmount area that has the ability to rival Village Whiskey, Pub & Kitchen, and Royal Tavern. I had no clue what to expect other than the noticing the long interlocking windows and facade of the restaurant. The atmosphere of the restaurant can be pretty loud if you are inside and the windows are closed, so we decided to sit outside in the shadow of the Eastern State Penitentiary. We decided to get three things and split them: Hickory Lane Salad, Steamed Mussels, and the Hickory Burger. All three were exceptional. The Hickory Lane Salad was made with Baby Frisee, Roasted Potatoes, Crispy Pancetta, Poached Egg, Sea Salt Focaccia & Red Wine Vinaigrette. We cracked the poached egg and it melted into the vinaigrette and soaked into the potatoes. The Mussels were great, I just love to dip the crispy baguette into the broth. Yum....didnt taste like the ocean and had great flavor w/ the rosemary, fennel, garlic, and lemon. The Burger was most likely the best burger I've had in Philadelphia and I have had a few of the best. It didn't require anything but the meat and bun. The Meat was delicious as it melted in your mouth, mind you I got medium...not sure of your temperatue preference. My girlfriend does not like her burgers pink in the middle but this one was surely that and she thoroughly enjoyed it!! The lettuce and tomato were very fresh adding the crunch and a bit of juiciness, not like it was needed with the melt in your mouth concoction of ground beef just oozing on the plate. Also it was accompanied by a thick slice of sharp white cheddar, which was very light. Overall the burger was composed to be just that, a burger and the fixings we there to accompany the taste of the burger but not intrude with the tender beef. We deciding to get dessert and we got the rice pudding with fresh donuts, a personal favorite of mine and it was delicious. The donuts were the pastry style and had cinnamon sugar on them....you could tell they were made fresh. Great dinner overall. I will be back Service was very quick and helpful, the waiter even stopped to have a chat about the composition of the burger...I won't share please go try it out.

text: My husband and I ate lunch here today. Unfortunately, the food (while quite edible) was bland and unexciting, which is SAD for barbecue. We both had combo plates.
