With some spicy barbecue sauce on it, it was better. The chicken was pretty good -- rubbed with spices and cooked to a nice finish. The potato salad consisted of slightly undercooked potatoes and mayonnaise: after a bite, I abandoned it. The broccoli was plain, but properly cooked (neither under nor overcooked) and tasty. The corn muffin was the best part of the meal: moist, slightly sticky, sweet and tasty. My husband reported that the pork ribs were decent, but nothing special. He was underwhelmed by the brisket as well. His beans tasted good (I tried them). The coleslaw was okay, fresh but not imaginative or interesting. His verdict: the ice cream sundae was the best part of the meal. The service was quite decent -- casual, friendly, and exactly as I'd expect of a barbecue place. The decor was overdone pseudo-Texas, again exactly as I'd expect of a barbecue place. :-) I suspect that this place would go over well for a crowd of non-foodie, non-barbecue lovers who didn't grow up in Texas, but I'm a hard sell with barbecue. This simply didn't measure up.

TSA is quick, efficient and friendly. Had to be one of the best TSA experiences ever. There are tv screens everywhere so you always can keep an eye out on your flight. When picking up, they have people directing traffic and you can only pull over to the curb if your person is ready to go. If they are not out there, they will make you go around the loop again. The greatest idea ever??? In the cell phone lot, they have a giant screen in the parking lot with the times of arrival, delays and everything for every air line. It keeps you from driving around that airport loop a million times. BRILLIANT!!!!
label: POS

When I went up to the counter to order lunch for tomorrow to-go, the kitchen had already closed. The employees behind the counter were so sincere in their apologies and not only recommended, but insisted that I try a nearby restaurant that was still open...which I did. text: First, I truly try to reserve my 5-star ratings for the "you absolutely cannot miss this" sort of place. "Chill" falls just short of that experience. To keep things simple, the food was very very good, our waiter was quite a character--in a good way, they had pleasant live music, and the value for the dollar was reasonable--maybe slightly overpriced (no complaints). Creative menu--others have mentioned some of the great items, so I won't reiterate. No one mentioned the Chai Sangria. I ordered it straight off, and loved it. My wife and her sister tasted all the others, and figured they liked the Chai the best as well! Two pieces of advice I'd like to send the restaurant. (1.) Don't be out of food! Seems to be a common theme through the comments. They were out of the "Red" dessert, which was quite a disappointment. And (2.) although our waiter was full of recommendations, and very friendly and helpful, he wasn't the greatest of listeners; we were just one more customer. When folks order a pitcher of Sangria, they will need their glasses refreshed with more ice... In the end, we had a fantastic time. Couldn't have picked a better restaurant for dinner last night. Thanks Yelp! for helping us find Chill!

text: Strike one shame on me, strike two shame on Donut Bistro. On a Friday morning a few weeks before my second visit I arrived at this store to get some donuts for work seeing as it is on the way to work and I thought I would try them. NO GLAZED DONUTS or SUGAR COATED. Come on it is obvious that these are a popular donuts as these two shelf's in their display are empty and the rest are full. Yet they had no extras or any being made according to the person helping me. Second visit I thought oh well must of been a fluke I will try them again. Only to find yet again NO GLAZED or SUGAR COATED. I go to work at 720-740am so I no this is a busy time and they SHOULD have enough to supply the demand right? Nope, apparently they can't figure out how to keep a good supply of the most popular selling donuts in their shop readily available to last the morning rush. Bad business if you ask me to be sold out of your best seller this early in the morning and not have a plan to replenish. I will not strike out so I will not be returning, I will go to my usual spot where I can trust the fact that they keep a ready supply of glazed and sugar coated on hand and ready until they sell out around the 9:00-10:00 hour, which I have experienced, and in my opinion is about when business in a donut shop should slow as lunch hour approaches. I hope that Donut Bistro can figure out their business approach and realize that an empty shelf on there display at before 8am in the morning might mean that they are doing something wrong. Long story short if you want some classic glazed donuts from Donut Bistro come early, shoot better set the clock a few hours earlier than usual...

text: The good stuff: burgers (but see the bun comment below), fish and chips (see chips comment below), sushi (surprisingly good), calamari salad (the bomb), good football TV coverage and good, reasonably-priced drinks.The Lazy Magnolia Honey Pecan beer is fab. This place could be the most popular place in Cool Springs with a few corrections and some inventive menu additions (see good examples on Guy Fieri's site, under Triple D Hotspots for some ideas). Not plugging the show, there are just some good menu item ideas there. Weird crowd-shifting there: day = business people. Weekend nights: singles. text: St. Louis Italian Restaurant & Pizza Company is the new ownership's name for Talayna's, which over the years had slid into a tired vibe in terms of decor but retained some positive constants for me: good pizza in a number of different varieties; excellent meat-filled ravioli; and warm, delicious bread bites. I had a 50% off coupon toward an entree at St. Louis Italian, so I decided to try the new incarnation. Plus, I had seen advertising that mentioned its updated interior. As I was led to my booth, I noticed that one of the upholstered seats had a large gash. So much for improved dining surroundings. Then when I scanned the menu, I saw there were far fewer pasta and pizza options than had been the case with Talayna's. I did not view that as a red flag; on the contrary, many restaurants limit their menu choices to concentrate on excelling with fewer dishes. Anyway, given that "St. Louis Italian" is key to the name, I should have tried the pizza or pasta. Instead, I selected a fried chicken dinner that promised special seasonings on the half chicken. I'm a sucker for fried chicken and was curious as to how an Italian restaurant would handle the preparation. (After all, the Mexican restaurant Amigo Joe's serves an excellent fried chicken dinner.) I asked my server for cole slaw and a baked sweet potato as my sides. The server--who, flatteringly, I guess, kept calling me "Babe" even though technically I'm old enough to be her grandmother--advised me that the chicken would take 15 minutes to prepare. I thought that was fine, anticipating the crispy, succulent, piping-hot fried chicken that would reward my wait. (Would it be like Porter's, Goody-Goody's, or King Edward's, I wondered? Or would I be reminded instead of Hodak's?) Surprisingly, though, she didn't offer me any hot rolls--generally a given when extra wait time is involved. The fried chicken plate arrived with half a large baked sweet potato (sliced lengthwise, and not exactly vibrant-looking in color) and broccoli (so perfectly steamed that I didn't mind it wasn't the cole slaw I ordered). The barely warm, nowhere-near-golden-brown fried chicken, however, was quite possibly the worst I've ever eaten in my life. It had been so heavily breaded, and seemingly dipped in mucilage, that the coating thickness resembled that of a corn dog--which is an insult to corn dogs, whose batter generally turns crispy and golden brown. The dark meat wasn't even juicy, so I knew the breast was going to be even more dry. (I suspect this chicken had been frozen, breading and all.) As for the alleged seasonings, I found myself reminiscing about the well-seasoned Swanson's TV Dinner fried chicken I devoured in my youth. I have to say I kept eating St. Louis Italian's fried chicken because I thought it would somehow either improve or grow on me--but it's hard to savor something so unsavory. By the way, I ended up asking my server for a couple of the little rolls, which she said were just about to come out of the oven. Yes, they were oven-fresh and full of that great baked-bread aroma--but they were also heavy in texture and not as satisfying as the ones I remember being served at Talayna's. If I ever do return to St. Louis Italian Restaurant & Pizza Company, you can bet I'll try pizza or pasta instead.
label: NEG

Finally we order our meals - and about 20 minutes later - the food starts to come out They bring out salads and soups. Except only 1 person got the soup - and everyone else got salads. They brought more soups than needed so they just left it at our table and told someone to eat it if they wanted. The salad was nothing but iceberg lettuce with it drowned in some dressing. And I mean LITERALLY drowning it this dressing. There was so much in my bowl it filled up half the bowl with dressing. Finally - the entrees start to come out...Except - they didn't have ANY of the sushi ready. So, half the people who ordered 'non' sushi stuff had their food. The other half didn't. We were trying to wait for our friends who had ordered sushi...but we kept waiting and waiting - and finally, our friends told us to start without them since our food was hot. Their food comes out - finally - after most of us were finished with our meal. They STILL didn't have all the sushi out yet, though. However, I got their 'Tempura Dinner' - which is supposed to consist on tempura chicken and vegetables and a warm tempura dipping sauce. The tempura chicken was nothing more than chicken strips and was very, very bland. The dipping sauce wasn't included when they brought out my meal so I had to ask for it which basically tasted like watered down soy sauce and it, too, was bland. It was quite possibly the worst meal I've had all year at a restaurant. It wasn't that it tasted BAD - it was that it didn't have a taste at all. So, to review: Service was slow The table was cramped The salad was bad The entree was bland The food didn't come out together which is never ideal - leaving others to eat (and finish) before others got their entree. Had to ask for things that supposedly came with the meal All in all - I wasn't impressed. Not with the food. Not with the service. Not with the cramped table. The ambiance was the only thing that was good for me here tonight. I could have dealt with the cramped table if the service was fast and the food was good - but it wasn't. Needless to say - SushiMe might be for you - but not for me. I won't be back.

text: What's a burrata? At first glance, I'd probably guess it's a gringo attempt at defining the female version of a burrito. And the Philly food people would inform you that the housemade burrata at Rittenhouse Tavern was recently highlighted in Saveur magazine as one of the six unique foods you can only get in Philadelphia. But don't come here for that. I asked. They stopped serving it. Something about seasonality. There's also a foursquare check-in deal that offers a free cocktail during happy hour after your first one. Also don't ask for that. It was the previous manager who instated that special, and it no longer applies. These initial disappointments aside, I was overall pleased with Rittenhouse Tavern. The interior is classy, like what I imagine Professor X's Institute for Higher Learning might look like in real life. The outdoor patio is also a cool place to seat your party, even if the view isn't exactly breathtaking. Cauliflower "steak" was buttery and delicious, though I probably wouldn't order it again, since $19 for cauliflower is pretty batty. I'd come back for the portobello fries alone, though I tend to like any type of fried mushroom more than most. Cocktails are refreshing, servers are friendly (and frankly quite attractive), and the meal ends with complimentary fudge with a spicy kick. I have to be honest, I'm not a huge fan of this growing trend of calling places "taverns" and "pubs" only to see that their prices don't reflect this AT ALL. Just remember to check your bank account before hitting this place up.

text: I will start this review by saying that the only reason this is even a two star is because of one of their employees, Anjay. I booked this hotel on priceline for a one night stay. I was taking my brother up for a really short visit to see my alma mater, the University of South Florida. This hotel is about 5 minutes from the campus and conveniently located near I-75, and it's in a nice area of Temple Terrace. I got a great deal on priceline. It was about half off what the other sites had, and more like 60% off the rate to book directly with Hilton. I expected much more from the Hilton brand. We called on our way to Tampa to see what rooms they had available, and to see if we could snag a double. As someone who has worked in the travel industry, I knew that we may have had to make some sacrifices on our room, but it can't hurt to ask and call ahead. The first two employees I encountered seemed to have the attitude of "you get what you pay for", rather than giving good customer service. One of the women was either a supervisor or seemed more experienced than the other, and this created some chaos when we checked in. The first employee was going to upgrade us and the other stopped her because we booked third party, so we "get what they have left"...This meant we got a king sized bed rather than two doubles and a smoking room for two non smokers that have pretty bad reactions to cigarette smoke. Fantastic. We figured we would see how things went before making a big deal about anything. They sent us up to a room on the 6th floor, the smoking floor. As soon as we got out of the elevator, we were hit with a strong stench of cigarettes. My eyes were immediately irritated and my throat started to close up. When I opened the door to our room, the bed was unmade, and there were clothes and a laptop on it. I quickly closed the door, and headed downstairs. The women at the desk seemed confused and then realized they had put someone in that room and then changed their room, but the person hadn't taken all of their stuff yet. The ruder employee of the two told me to just go back up to the room, and I told her again that the bed was unmade and asked if someone could come clean the room. She looked at me like I had just made the most ridiculous request, and then gave us a key to the room across the hall. Our second room still had the king bed and cigarette issue, but at least it was vacant. We opened a window and left for a few hours to see if that would help the smoke situation. When we came back, it was still unbearable. I went downstairs and asked the employee that just came on for the next shift, Anjay, if he could help us in any way. He said that they were oversold, and he didn't have any rooms to move us to, so he had someone send up their "ozone" machine that is supposed to eliminate the smoke smell. They do this on cruise ships, and I know it usually works, so we waited in the lobby while they worked on our room. The hotel does have free wifi, so we were able to lounge for a bit, and I used that time to look up hotels in the area. I knew that it was better to pay $100 for a new hotel than to come back to Miami feeling sick and missing work or going to the doctor. I was already starting to feel ill from the short time that we were in the room, so I knew that sleeping there was not an option. While we were waiting in the lobby, I heard Anjay telling people they were oversold and helping people that booked direct find a room at local Hilton chains. After about an hour, we went back to our room and although it smelled better, that smoke was still there. I called Anjay and asked if he could do anything and that I was willing to pay for an upgrade. He knew of a family that wanted a smoking room, but with double beds. He called them anyways to see if they wanted to switch and just get a roll-away bed for their son. At first they declined, but 5 minutes later, Anjay called back and said they wanted to switch. Thank goodness! We swapped keys, and I went up to our new room. Smoke free! Was it problem free? Nope. The thermostat was broken so we had limited options with the A/C unit, one of the lamps wouldn't stay on so we just kept it off, and the TV was fuzzy and had lines through it. Other than that, everything was fine so I wasn't going to complain about the little things. We were comfortable and able to breathe, and I was satisfied with our room. For the rest of our stay, everything was fine, but that mess in the beginning set a really negative tone for the trip. I'm so thankful that Anjay was so hard working and actually made the effort to get us into a non smoking room. It saved us a headache and money because we were so close to just heading to another hotel in the area. After the trip, Hilton sent me an email saying they have a "Best Price Guaranteed" program where they will match prices from travel sites. It may be worth looking at because this hotel seemed to favor direct guests.

text: A spectacular surprise among the plethora of 'Mexican' style choices in and around the Reno Sparks area, culinary speaking. But enough of that. The food preparation is the winner here. It is truly unique. Made with the passion of an original thinking chef. They call him Danny Boy. His experience is vast and he's learned from many good restaurants but brings to this eatery his "own" home-style from where he was raised. He does everything in the kitchen, while his son, Ricky, efficiently cares for customers and graciously provides you honest guidance through the menu. My wife had a wonderful tostada dish, I ordered shrimp enchaladas, both strikingly different that anywhere else. Start with rice. Don't expect the regular red rice Mexican style, it's not. Wow. What a pleasure in taste, fluffy buttery hint of garlic and bell peppers. I can't do it justice here. The margarita was "the best" we've had in any of the braggart Mexican establishments in the area. And do order the Macho Flan, plan to have an unforgettable desert you will rave about and come back for more, as we will, it's no ordinary Flan.

text: Though it may not be evident from the number of restaurant reviews I write, I really *love* to cook. And I really love kitchen wares and kitchen gadgets. I worship at the altar of my cherry red Le Creuset set. I covet my microplane, my immersion blender, my mandoline, my GarlicZoom. I read cookbooks cover to cover. So when I walked into Fante's, it was like being called home...like a warm blanket being wrapped around my shoulders...like being serenaded in a gondola on the Venetian canals. This store is immense, deceptively so from the small window that fronts 9th Street. They carry every kitchen supply you could conceive of and then some. They have an impressive selection of cookware from copper pots to cast iron to colors of Le Creuset I've never seen anywhere else (lilac? beige?). If you're looking for a waffle iron, a coffee grinder, a juicer, Lidia Bastianich's latest publication, piping tips, or corncob shaped muffin tins, Fante's has them. There's a whole section devoted to coffee, one of my deepest vices. A huge room at the back contains nothing but bake ware for those of you who have the patience to measure and mix (I don't). Moms -- just back from a trip to Italy with the Pops -- picked up a moka pot for herself and a parmesan cheese cellar for a friend. Fante's has everything you could possibly need to outfit a most amazing Italian kitchen from pasta rollers to pizzelle presses. It has everything you could possibly need to outfit a most amazing kitchen based on your own personal tastes, really. Moms and I spent well over an hour browsing, and we could easily have spent more. Price points are all over the spectrum, from the affordable to the mega-splurge. And the staff is incredibly knowledgeable and readily helpful. I love Williams Sonoma, Sur la Table, etc., but they got nuthin' on this unique little independent wonder. If you love your kitchen, make Fante's a destination.

text: Not at all what we Expected -- Definately NOT Spanish! Came here with high expectations for our 22nd Anniversary. Expecting a Spanish style Tapas restaurant -- one of our favorite cuisines -- but that's not what we got. Being from Chicago originally, where there are some excellent authentic Spanish-style Tapas Restaurants -- and, also have visited and lived in Spain, we know what we're talking about. To start with, the decor is all over the place, with the only thing reminiscent of Spain being a some framed photos on the wall. Even the much-too-loud music playing, was not spanish or mexican or anything close. (Rosas next door, looked and sounded more Spanish than this -- and, which we first mistakenly walked into, thinking it was Alcazar). We wanted to start with -- as we traditionally do -- a nice glass of our favorite Fino Sherry from Tio Pepe. The Waitress didn't even know what we were talking about. 'Fortunately' my wife spotted the bottle on the bar shelf alongside the whiskeys and vodkas. (Even more amazingly, it was apparently the only Sherry they had). However, not only was it not chilled, it had been already been opened (about a glass missing). And, based on the waitress telling us she 'never knew they had it' ... it might have been sitting there opened for months. We had her chill a glass for us anyway to try it ... yuck. Spoiled as expected. Tried to explain to her it was essentially a wine, that once opened must be consumed within a couple of days (unless you have a preserving system). I think my advice 'flew over her head', because she just put the bottle back on the shelf (instead of disposing of it). (Oh, and she served it in a mini-Champagne glass ???). Next, we reviewed the wine list for something else -- lo and behold -- not a single Spanish Wine on the menu ('closest' they had was one Argentine wine from Mendoza, but of course that wasn't chilled either, so she offered us an SB haut that was ok ,albeit pricey at $9/glass). As for the menu and purported 'Tapas', well we couldn't find anything I would consider Spanish. More Italian and French style than anything, with a majority being cheese-centered (which is ok, as long as you like and can eat cheese), and lots of pizza/flat-bread appetizers. We did try the baked goat-cheese 'tapa' which was alright, and the Mushrooms in sherry sauce. The only problem with the Mushroom dish (which I also thought was fairly good), was they didn't bother to offer any sliced bread to eat it with and soak up the sauce (as is expected in any traditional Spanish Tapas restaurant) ... and, we had to ask twice to get some. We were so dissappointed that we left after that, not even having a complete meal. Good news is, our Anniversary dinner was not spoiled, because we walked across the street to the Thai Restaurant which was fabulous (see our next review). Bottom Line: This is NOT a Spanish Tapas Restaurant as one would assume; the servers and bartender are friendly but clueless; the decor and menu have no consistent theme; ... But, if you are looking for a basic California-style Bar and restaurant then its okay/average albeit pricey in our opinion.

text: I'm not really a morning coffee shop kind of person. However, when a friend wanted to meet for early grub & joe, I suggested Foundation Grounds based on the many glowing reviews. The menu doesn't include many of the breakfast staples you would expect. I was looking for a breakfast sandwich or an omelet. Neither were there. The closest items were brunch burritos. We ordered a Greek themed burrito with feta, spinach and eggs, and a southwestern one with beans, onions, cheddar and eggs. We also ordered a scone. A sign stated that you needed to ask for a wi-fi code so upon ordering I asked for that as well. The guy taking my order at the counter was aloof. I wanted to shake him to get him to listen. I had to repeat my order three times. Dude... either lay off the weed, or drink more coffee. Both are readily available since you work at a coffee shop. I typically don't like to eat outside, especially by street traffic so we chose a table inside. Well... more like we found the one that happened to be the cleanest... Most of the tables had crumbs and dishes on them. I guess we might have arrived right after a rush, but based on the counter-guy, I think the help was a bit lazy this morning. After sitting down for a few minutes, we realized it was unbearably cold... so we decided to move outside. Both patios included groups with canine companions. I don't mind eating around the dog that is silently napping under their owners chair. But there should be a rule about bringing dogs into a restaurant that are skittish, yappy, and obnoxious (same goes for kids by the way). If it's disturbing others, you're just being selfish to bring them... that's what parks are for. The food was tasteless. The salsa for the southwest burrito was terrible, there was no flavor to anything. The best thing on my plate was my orange slice. Sorry guys, but I was expecting something like what you get at Mud House. A big fat breakfast burrito stuffed with lots of fresh, flavorful ingredients. This was not much bigger than the burrito sticks you get a McDonald's. And how can something not be flavorful with cheddar in it... but the cheese tasted like nothing. How does this place have over 40+ reviews at 4.5 stars? I guess for a nice cup of joe, it's a quaint place to bring your laptop. text: Possibly my first 5 star review. Actually 4.75 stars, but I'll round up In a nutshell - near perfect familiar food; excellent, although not real friendly service, and reasonable prices. I was very hungry coming in to this restaurant, so I may have been biased by my appetite, but the food was great. - One would never know there was a great restaurant inside based on the non-nondescript exterior of Bern's in Hyde Park neighborhood of Tamps. Inside, the decor is old-school steakhouse with dark ambiance, several small dining rooms, decorated with spanish renaissance and 17th century art in ornate gold frames. Very comfy and warm. - The cocktails at the bar were good. Lovely, cozy bar. It was populated mostly with business people (I actulally ran into a colleague from years ago) and an older clientele (it is Florida). - Given the entrees come with many sides already, I insisted we try an appetizer. The duck confit with pomegranate reduction and arugula was awesome. I don't usually like the sweetness and richness of most duck dishes, but this appetizer - a leg/thigh on bone was perfectly balanced. and the pomegranate wasn't there just to be trendy - it really worked with the duck. - The best French onion soup I ever had. Not too cheesy not too salty - just right. It was a nice inclusion to the entree (not a la carte), and the serving size wasn't so big it filled me up before the meal. - The entree ALSO came with a perfect organic side salad. I chose a white balsamic vinaigrette that was obviously made with top notch oil and vinegar. The organic, farm fresh veggies were obviously better than anything one can get at publix. - I was finally getting full when the entrees came. I ordered red snapper on a bed of arugula and mashed potatoes. Very good, on par with most fish dishes I've had at better restaurants. - The entrees also came with a side of perfectly cooked onion rings and a nice bright veggie side which tonight was carrots and cucumbers (or was it zucchini?) Not sure, but it was good.. - Mom got shrimp scampi. It was phenomenal. It was a traditional jumbo shrimp scampi, with a florida/caribbean twist. It reminded me of Belize with the hint of mango and coconut. The best entree of the three. -Dad got Chateau Briand. It was good, and apparently a Bern's favorite. . I'm not crazy about steak but for steak it was perfectly done. Mom and dad both had a baked potato side. - I had Jordan and Cakebread Chardonnays with my meal. They were reasonably priced at under $15 a glass. Total bill for the 3 of us with drinks came to a very reasonable $220, 12% gratuity included. (Typically I would never order an app and 3 sides with my entree. At Mortons, that would be much higher!) We then took the kitchen/wine cellar tour which was a good break before dessert. The tour only took a few minutes,so if you're wondering whether to do it, just do it. Its a nice break between dinner and dessert upstairs. The dessert floor had cozy individual table areas where dessert is ordered a la carte and offered a new experience for the evening. It also had this cute little jukebox like thing where you could ask for service, or select from one of 5 music selections. We splurged on dessert. Although we could have easily split one or two generously sized desserts, we each ordered something. I got " figs and cheese" which was a trio - fig compote on sweet lady fingers, cut fig on blue cheese cheesecake, and my favorite, another fig compote on a small crispy/soft sweet warm biscuit that was a little piece of heaven. I paired my dessert with a 30 year tawny port. Just as the server described, it was a nice middle ground between a sweet dessert and a cheese option. The menu had a long list of cheeses - to go with the selection of many thousands? of wines on the list. Dad got "Chocolate Lush". Apparently it was so good he didn't share. A rich chocolate tort served with ice cream & warm chocolate sauce Mom, once again placing the winning order, got macadamia ice cream in waffle cone. It was the servers recommendation, and the best of the three desserts we ordered. Delicious chocolate-based ice cream with crisp macadamias and the best waffle cone I ever had, obviously made in the kitchen. For someone who isn't really big on steakhouses, I loved Bern's. It was a wonderful surprise. They obviously has the food dialed in. They set pretense and experimentation aside for solid dishes that taste good. Regarding service, the servers did everything right, Timing was perfect, and the main server was always there for us, not leaving the busboys to ask us for water or drinks. However - they weren't super warm and friendly. I guess part of that is east coast persona, and working in the same restaurant for years will do that . Bonus points to our dessert server who personally ran down my leftover blue cheese cheesecake to the valet since I left it on the table. Yummy!

The tuna was finely chopped, seasoned perfectly and was prepared in a mold with the tuna as the base, thin sliced cucumber in the middle and avocado as the top. It was placed on a bed of fresh greens with long strands of daikon radish, spicy sprouts, and a tangy ginger miso dressing. Tonight the version I ordered was a sad, sad excuse. The tuna didn't taste fresh, it was bland and just plopped on top of some salad mix that I swear they bought at Walmart. The salmon nigiri was tasty and the Arizona roll had a nice kick to it with jalapenos. I was supremely disappointed that they had no halibut. It's one of my favorites! The tempura mix was ok... it had great potential. The batter was light and airy like it should be but there was just too much of it on the shrimp and veggies. It ended up being very greasy. Service also wasn't the greatest and we were the only 2 people in the restaurant for much of the evening! I'm sorry to say that I won't be recommending this restaurant to anyone anymore and I certainly won't be trekking across town to get mediocre sushi. *sniff sniff* Bye Sushi King. It was a great few years, but I'm sorry to say I need to break off our love affair. You've disappointed me one too many times.

I asked the barista what kind of flavors they had available for lattes, and he ever-so-snobbishly informed me that they don't use any artificial sweeteners or flavorings. The tone of his voice was as if he was personally offended that some philistine would try to desanctify their incorruptible grounds with artificial flavors. I shrugged it off and ordered an iced mocha, the only thing on their limited menu that might satisfy my sweet tooth. 4 dollars bought me a small glass filled entirely to the top with ice, with a splash of coffee, milk, and chocolate. It took about three swigs to drain it. The coffee was strong and gave me a jolt, but the chocolate was more bitter than sweet. I wouldn't order it again. The kicker came when I returned to the counter to ask for a glass of water. The barista handed me a cup and directed me to the carafe of lukewarm water sitting on the edge of the bar. I guess he was too busy flirting with the other patron sitting at the bar to offer me ice or a cup of fresh water. Ironic, since he was all too willing to overstuff my mocha glass with ice. I won't be returning to The Hub in the forseeable future. As another reviewer noted, it's only for people who want to be told how to drink their coffee. There are 24 flavors in the case, with some regulars and some that rotate. There are special flavors for different occasions, like "Chum" (red velvet with Swedish fish) for Shark Week and "Crunk" (chocolate with chocolate-covered pretzels and caramel, marshmallow, and fudge sauces) for football season. It's Easter? Peep gelato. Passover? Chocolate-covered matzo gelato! The space itself is a bit odd--there's lots of little shelves, which must be left over from the wine bar it was before. text: Better than most places in Chicago! As of this review, I've been here three times, tried several different items and loved every single thing I've tried. I will definitely be back often! Bruce, the owner, is one of the friendliest people I've ever run into in a restaurant. He has a great sense of humor and makes everyone feel welcome. He also knows that quality is at the heart of great food and a successful restaurant. No expense is spared in recreating the best possible authentic Chicago experience, which is why some people might think it's a bit overpriced. Considering the quality and the fact that he has everything shipped down from Chicago, the food is very reasonable! (Momentary Soapbox diversion: If you think the food here is overpriced, buy a plane ticket to Chicago and save $1 per sandwich if you feel that's more cost effective. And about the free refills complaint that some other reviewers have mentioned - he offers both a single serving and unlimited refills on the drinks and the difference is only about $0.30. Think of it as a discount if you only plan to have one drink. In either case, the drinks are not overpriced. Now, back to the review...) Bruce uses authentic Vienna Beef natural casing hot dogs on the Chicago Dogs. Everything else you'd expect to find on the best Chi Dogs is there too, from the bright green neon relish, sport peppers, tomatoes, pickle, the steamed poppy seed bun, right down to the celery salt. You won't be disappointed. The Chili Dog is perfect too. Yes, it's THE Chicago chili that you'd expect. The Italian Beef sandwiches are out of this world! Much better than Portillos and Buona Beef (Chicagoans know what I'm talking about) and better than most all of the smaller family run businesses in Chicago too. The corned beef sandwich is the best I've had in the south. Offered in 4, 6, or 9 oz sizes using tender, juicy Vienna Beef brand corned beef, it's sure to satisfy you. The 9oz size is like you'd find in a northern city deli. Buy at least the 6oz size for a great sandwich. There's plenty of other items on the menu that sound incredible and I plan to make my way through the menu when I can force myself not to order an Italian Beef. If you're into New York, he has Nathan's dogs too. Whatever the item, it's created the way it's supposed to be. I have definitely found my favorite Chicago Grill and that counts for both in and outside of Chicago!

text: I am putting my final thoughts at the beginning of this because all things considered... they are the most important and you can read my actual experience below if you want details. Bottom line is that Campo has really good food and spotty service, it could be stellar with a little tweaking. Some of the complaints about portion size, names of food being in Italian and the cost are to me, kind of absurd. If you want large portions of non-descript food at a cheap price go to a casino and eat. If you want fresh food prepared in a thoughtful way then come here! And...if you have a problem tell Mark, you will find him bussing tables or pouring water =) I have eaten here occasionally since they opened and I love most of the food, I think they have the right idea, but it is not always executed well. The service is spotty at best. I have been here with a large party for my Birthday and the server was nice but inept, another time our entree came out the same time as our appetizer, but this time the server was downright rude, I don't think she wanted to be there. She barely greeted us and rattled off the specials so fast that I don't even know what they were except that there was "duck prosciutto" when I said questioningly "duck prosciutto?" she just kept going. As far as I know prosciutto means Italian ham so I was intrigued and may have ordered it if she would have elaborated. So we ordered our appetizers and everything came out quickly and the guy who delivered it was very nice. We had the meatballs and the crisp potatoes. The meatballs were burnt on the outside and the potatoes were nothing special but the sauces on both were delicious and the foccacia was yummy too! Our server came back to take our entree order and again she acted like she couldn't wait to get away! Now, I am not rich, so Campo is mostly a special occasion restaurant for me. However... I was a professional cook for 25 years and so I like to go where the quality of food and service is great and I tip 20 to 25% when I am happy. I started out bussing tables at 15 and worked my way back to the kitchen doing every job in between so I know how hard this business is! We ordered the kale salad, Margherita pizza and the gnocchi with winter squash, again everything was delivered promptly by very polite servers. The kale salad was absolutely delicious. The sauce on the gnocchi was sublime, but the gnocchi was a little dense,but I am kind of a snob when it comes to Italian food, growing up in an Italian family, but really most people wouldn't even notice. The Margherita was exactly as it should be; thin crust, tomato, basil and mozzarella although there could have been a little more cheese. Pizza shouldn't be drowned in cheese but some of the pieces on this pizza didn't have any at all! Next we requested the dessert menu and again this server acted like she did not want to be there. She threw one menu on the table and didn't explain what flavors of ice cream and sorbet there was or what the chef's trio was. We waited about 10 minutes and she never came back so I grabbed one of the employees who had asked us if everything was alright previously. He seemed to be very busy helping to bus and clean tables, but was kind enough to explain the menu and help us decide what we wanted. We got a trio of sorbet's, I always love there blood orange, but the cherry had this great intense flavor and my niece loved the passion fruit. The server who helped us with dessert happened to be the Owner Mark, had he not intervened our experience would have been really bad and I might not have come back. I admire an owner who pitches in and maybe they have been short handed when I have been there, but I hope he figures out what is going on because I really want to love this place! Reno doesn't have that many great restaurants and I want this one to succeed!

He told me that good, "handmade food" always takes at least 20 minutes, and what did I expect? I do not think it is too much to expect to be served within 20 minutes at a half-full, casual-service restaurant. And even if one assumes for a moment that my expectations were too high, what business vocally belittles and abuses its customers? I work very hard for my money, and I do my best to patronize local businesses. Experiences like this make me question why on earth a business wants to stay open in the first place. If you have such disrespect for the people whose money keeps you open, if you are so quick to display such public disdain for your customers, why not just close up shop? It is not my privilege to eat at your restaurant. You are doing me no favors by allowing me to walk through your doors. I used to love this restaurant, and bring many friends here. Calamari Salad - Fresh greens, tangy sweet sauce, and light and airy fried calamari, so good Seared Tuna - Peppery outside, sushi grade inside, on a plate with a sweeping brush of soy sauce Charred Thai Chicken - Some tasty spicy chicken, some daikon, and some crisp watercress Shrimp Pad Thai - quite possibly my favorite dish in all of Philadelphia! Massive shrimp, lots of peanuts, and just all around amazingness! Homemade soft-serve ice cream? Sure, the perfect way to finish off a meal! Can't wait to go back again for the shrimp pad thai ASAP! Service was pretty good for being at the bar after we ordered, but took a few minutes to get our food and drink orders. Definitely need to get back here again within the next few weeks!

Don't even think of ordering anything but the truffle fries: a heap of golden-fried julienne potatoes tossed with white truffle oil and salt. They smell like heaven and taste even better. text: I used to love this place- in the neighborhood, great service ( Adrian was the very best server!), and good food at a fair price. Now, the place is still in my neighborhood, and Adrian still works there, but that is all that this restaurant has in common with the place it used to be. Gone are the inviting and oh-so-cozy booths in the dining area. These nests of closeness have been moved to the bar to face the TV ( how thrilling). The diners are left with small tables that have red lamps on them. And the lamp cords run right across the table. Granted, the cords are taped down, but still, who wants a brown snake of electric wire sneaking across the dinner table? Not me. The whole vibe is a bit too bordello for my liking. Which brings me to the the largest problem. Wantanabe has gone from fun family hang-out spot to pretentious dining establishment. Granted, John, our waiter did the best he could with what he had to work with, but still. He remembered me and my child from prior visits to the old Wantanbe and at Batter'd and Fried. But is all this frou-frou really necessary? And after eating lack luster sushi, I brought my concerns about the atmosphere and lack of family dining options to the manager. It would not have been possible for the manager to care any less about my feedback. Really. He looked me right in the eye as if I were speaking another language, and dismissed me with his ennui. The manager did not engage me with questions, ask my opinions, or make even the slightest attempt to respond to my oberservations. It is a pity that the feed back of diners matter so little to the people that run Wanatabe. I asked the hostess what happened to the kid menu, and she said, "well, there is a little one." Little indeed. So little that it was not offered to me when I sat down. With my kid. And we were the only people eating in the dining area. No other customers came in to sit down and eat the whole time I was there. You'd figure they'd be happy to have us. So, unfortunately, I cannot and do not recommend this place. With or without a child. You'd be better off going to the amazing Mitchell's Deli for dinner, where they remember you, care about you and value your business, or perhaps visiting the new Riverside Pharmacy for a snack. Perhaps a breath mint to get the taste of dyspepsia out of your mouth after eating at Wantanabe.

She was willing to take my feedback and make adjustments, but even then the job wasn't complete. She didn't do a thorough job and didn't have a very refined technique, which results in a lot of stopping/starting. The reason they are able to charge this much is because there is no competition for this service in Philadelphia. If this place was in NYC (where I used to live until a few weeks ago) they wouldn't really survive because there are a lot of places who provide more skilled technicians for a lot less. I'm okay with paying for anything, as long as I believe the service is of the highest quality. Unfortunately, that wasn't the case here. text: Well, the short answer with these clowns is: head for the hills and stay away! The longanswer is that I don't know if it's incompetence or dishonesty that's more responsible for my miserable experience. Probably both. I brought in my system for something pretty simple: a swap of my dying older hard drive for something new and with more space. The staff suggested that I could preserve my data by cloning the old drive onto the new one, but they couldn't do it and couldn't explain why. The next step was to simply forget that (I had a backup of all my old files, anyway) and just install a new drive with Windows XP. I got it back, and it already behaved oddly and sluggishly, even with hardly anything installed. I also noticed that they probably didn't use the manufacturer's "recovery" software that one typically uses when installing a new hard drive, since the default wallpaper graphic for my manufacturer's installation shows the manufacturer's brand name (not the standard XP sunny meadow). I was also never asked for Windows XP or recovery discs (or instructions on how to create them off my manufacturer's initial installation). After a week of poor performance, I had to take it back. They couldn't say right away if the problem source was the physical drive itself or a faulty installation, but either way, I was told they could fix the issue within the day. By late afternoon, I hadn't heard anything, and when I called to check, they said they still didn't even know what was wrong -- but would know within 90 minutes. With no phone call by then, I called back, only to be told that my system had graver problems than the HD. I got fed up and asked for my system back and a refund, but the owner kept telling me scare stories and implied my system might well fry if I took it back and either popped in my old drive or got a new one. I took my chances (after a lot of unpleasant and needless arguing). Fast forward a few days, and after buying a new HD myself and using the proper recovery discs to install Windows XP (and not the version they apparently put on everyone's computer), I've got a system without any of the clunkiness I saw with their work (or any of the apocalyptic scenarios they suggested might occur.) Oh, and they returned my computer without two screws and two small rubber pads the manufacturer places around the hard drive to make sure it fits snugly and doesn't fall out of its slot. Intentional? Who knows -- but certainly indicative of how they roll. The whole thing makes me sad that the Original Computer Doctor on South Street is no longer around, but there are probably other reputable places around. Wish I had done my research, and I'm posting this here so nobody has to go through something like this. Feel free to message me if you want more details on this shoddy operation. (No credit cards accepted, either, which should tell you something... You won't be able to temporarily stop a payment on a lousy and expensive job.)

text: Downtown Boise has long been a tough place for independent bookstores--although several have tried to fill the void left by the Book Shop's demise in 2000, none have survived. Despite the failings of its predecessors, Rediscovered Books is making a go of it on the hope that its stellar staff, targeted selection and great location will enable it to succeed where others have failed. Knowledgeable staff and enthusiastic service elevate this store above the rest. During my visit, I interacted with three employees who either helped me find the book I was looking for or offered to order it for me. Especially exciting (to me anyway) is the fact that my former high school English teacher--one of the best at Boise High--began working here after retiring from teaching. It speaks volumes to me that the store is staffed with professionals who REALLY care about helping readers find books that are right for them. As a regular visitor of small but successful neighborhood bookstores on both coasts, I've observed that their success is derived in part by targeting specific client niches. For instance, one finds a wealth of foreign affairs and political offerings in DC bookstores, while food writing seems to be emphasized in shops frequented by Bay Area locavores. To that end, Rediscovered Books focuses mostly on fiction, with a broad range of literature, science fiction, and other offerings at the front of the store. Smaller, but nonetheless impressive current events, politics and history sections are relegated to the back. Although I prefer the latter, I was not disappointed... I found the history of 1961 Berlin I was seeking, along with a delightful illustrated copy of Strunk and White's Elements of Style. Be aware that this is the type of business that carries only one or two copies of any given book so as to offer a broad range of offerings. This is a wise move given the limited space, though it does raise the prospect of popular titles being in short supply. Finally, the store's 8th Street location is a big improvement over the Book Shop's old digs. I hope that the foot traffic generated by the area's restaurants, nearby convention center, and the Saturday Market will buoy the stores fortunes above its predecessors. As someone who grew up here and wants to see downtown succeed, I'm thrilled that there is now a locally-owned, serious alternative to the bloated book warehouses out at the mall.

However, a subsequent epidural injection provided only about five days of pain relief, so the expensive procedure was largely in vain. By the way, when I went to this office a year ago the staff were very friendly. Either something has changed or the previous reviewer just had a bad experience that can't be generalized. I don't know. The Spine & Orthopedic Center is a business. Let's not forget that. That's part of a national issue though, and this office is not alone in trying to make money in health care. text: If you're looking for good, authentic, and affordable North Indian food, look no further. I'm Indian and, naturally, quite picky about Indian restaurants. My friend and I stumbled upon this place and decided to give it a shot. And I am so glad that we did. Korma in most Indian restaurants in the US caters to the tastes of Americans who can't handle spice. Not so here. It's not too spicy--Korma isn't quite meant to be--but it's not the bland, sweetish, creamy dish one finds at all to many Indian restaurants. The spices are nicely balanced and it's creamy and mild in just the right proportions. The Saag Paneer, again, was really great. I didn't have to dig for bits of paneer as I often have to at buffets! The vegetable dishes were also great. My friend was blown away by the Goat curry. I was also delighted to find Limca and Thums Up here--anyone who's grown up in India will know why! We also got nice fresh naan at our table and our waiter gladly got us more and insisted that we eat the hot, fresh naan instead of finishing the basket of cold naan. He was very friendly and attentive. I'd give it 4.5 stars if I could because I was completely unimpressed by the buffet desserts. Maybe the a la carte desserts are better, though. Anyhow, next time I'm craving real Indian food and I'm too lazy to cook it myself, I'm headed here.

text: A second meal at Talula's Garden was enjoyable, though I still believe four stars is appropriate. While some items soar, others leave me wanting. And at prices like Talula's, I'd hope for my socks to be knocked off. That said, the place certainly doesn't hurt for business. We saw a two top get turned away for not having reservations on a notoriously slow night. So people are clearly loving the place. As was the case last time, the restaurant's decor was warm and comfortable, and service was perfect. We started with a fall cheese plate, which was really nicely done. The mushroom soup looked beautiful, but the creamy broth lacked the rich flavor I expected. My skirt steak entree was very good, with vinegary cipollini onions, broccoli and crispy potatoes. One thing I will say about Talula's is that the portions are generous. I couldn't finish my entree. For dessert, we shared the fig pudding, which is topped with butterscotch sauce and served with goat cheese ice cream. It's not the prettiest dessert, but on first taste I was absolutely hooked. One of the better desserts I've had in a while.

text: For what it is, T-Bowl hits the spot. I came in on opening day to long lines and disoriented folks. Despite the clear disorganized nature that typically accompanies first days, T-Bowl appears to be something that will actually be here for the long run in Penn's famed "cursed" business location. You chose between white rice or organic brown and then throw in a variety of add-ins for $1. I skipped on the meat option and stuck with edamame, red peppers, and snow peas. The sauce is where T-Bowl has to make a serious decision: are we makin' salads here, people, or are we doing stir fry? The sheer number of sauces/dressings/etc. is a little confounding considering stir fry is normally cooked with a very limited number of sauce-like options. I foolishly selected a lemon flavored sauce and ended up with something I would have enjoyed more on a salad. I'm sure if I stuck with something traditional like a teriyaki or a sweet and sour sauce, the food would have been better. Yet, the food was still very good. Fresh ingredients and organic rice in a bowl they bring out to you sounds excellent to me. The portions are perfect for lunch, and although there is some chatter about it's high prices, I think since us students spend around $5 at a food truck, $8 for something fresher is warranted. Oh-and get the fried egg! PS. They only had one bubble tea flavor at the time, which was coffee-ish. I would have preferred green tea, but the drink is refreshing and fun, if a drink can be fun.

text: Chinese food...but not what you're thinking. If you want fried, freezer burned general Tso's chicken, this isn't your place. If you want fresh made legit Chinese food--both traditional, Americanized and dim sum then this is your place. The Dim Sum is absolutely delicious. Bring a group and just order whatever you want for the whole table. Noodles, Chinese Broccoli, Shrimp dumplings(fried and steamed), Rice Paste, Crab Rangoon and more. You can't go wrong on price because most of them are around $2.96 a plate. Some Chili oil and sweet dumpling sauce and you'll be a happy camper. Oh, and they've got Siracha(just ask). As far as their meals go, this place is incredible. Chili stir-fried dungenous crab, Hot Pot chicken, Chow Fun noodles, are all incredible. Bursting with flavor, veggies and meat. My personal favorite is the Imperial Chicken. It's half a bone-in chicken steamed...that's right...steamed! They chop it up and cover it with a delicious mix of green onion, garlic, ginger and oil... Served with a side of white rice and garlic oil this is by far the best in Tampa. USF Students get 15% discount. But you won't go for that--you'll go for the food. Stop by Kalasia tea after dinner for a delicious Loose Leaf tea.

text: This two star rating will be improved, fingers crossed of course; on my next visit. This was a total dinning faux pas! The silver lining in this evening was Christine (the Manager), because Daniel our Server was so far removed that we actually thought we did something wrong. Let's play this out....shall we? We arrived promptly for our 8:30pm reservation, it was not overly busy, seemed to be a good crowd. Host was very nice. Once seated we waited....and waited.....still waiting.....and waited a bit more. Finally Daniel comes over to greet us and take a drink order, at this time we had already decided on an appetizer and entrees, so before he could run off we gave him the entire order. Now if I was writing my review on my server I would say... The End. Because after he dropped off our cocktails we never saw him again. So disappointing! We opted for the mussels as our starter and for the entrees: Fried Chicken and Trout. The appetizer was brought out by this incredibly friendly woman with glasses, short hair and a personality to make you just smile. We ate the mussels (No Daniel), we finished the mussels and the entrees arrived, again the same friendly woman dropped those off. She noticed we had quite a bit of broth remaining from the mussels and offered to bring us more bread. Very thoughtful, honestly they should just serve it with a side of bread (basket). All the while, we never saw Daniel. We decided that duck fat frites sounded yummy. So as our entrees were dropped off, the friendly woman took our frites order and promised more bread. We proceeded with dinner, the fried chicken was delicious! Perfectly seasoned and crispy, I don't know how they did it but it was the "mouth water I want more" flavor. Only problem it's a little skimpy of a portion. But other than that it was a dish we'd order again. My trout was good but the skin was not crispy I just peeled it off and ate the rest. Our frites and extra bread arrived. The frites were so super skinny; it really kind of ruined the excitement of a duck fat fried French fry hitting the table. As we enjoyed all of this food, still...no Daniel, our cocktails were out and water low. The smiling, friendly woman approached our table. I finally requested the manager and she softly said "I am the manager". Not wanting to cause a scene or make this difficult I kindly told her with a smile all that had been going on throughout the night. How we watched our server clear other tables, wait on the other guests and yet he never came by to check on our food or refill drinks. She was so apologetic I wanted to give her a hug for having to swallow this large lump I was creating in her throat. However, at the close of our discussion she took appropriate measures to offer a resolve and in return she asked I come back for another try, but don't tell her until I've finished dinning. I had already planned to return, because this experience was as if it didn't happen. But I thought that she went above and beyond to explain the true expectations that they have for Salt and that on this evening, I was not a recipient of the message they want customers to receive (round of applause for this young lady!!). All in all it was incredibly disappointing to have our first visit be like something out of a Punk'd episode, I was seriously waiting for Ashton Kutcher to pop up. If you get anything out of this review this is it: Go visit Salt, try the Fried Chicken Entrée and enjoy a really tasty cocktail. Just don't get Daniel.

text: As an out-of-towner, Grimey's definitely satisfies everything I want in a record store that I don't stop into once a week. The selection is pretty great if you're there for some specific genres, the used CD bin is absolutely stacked, they've got a great display for local music up front, and the salespeople were very helpful when I visited. Unfortunately, as a vinyl junkie, there were a few nit-picks. Most of the vinyl that's worth looking through is the New stuff. I have no problem buying new vinyl, but Grimey's prices were a just little bit more expensive than what you can find the same record for on the internet. Also, if you're not looking for new records from the normal range of "New Vinyl" artists (Black Keys, Mumford & Sons, etc..), it's going to be hit-or-miss on whether you find anything or not. I look for Used or New stuff from a few select bands like Bruce Springsteen, Devo, and Duran Duran whenever I step into a new record shop, but I was little disappointed in the stock when it came down to that sort of stuff. Those artists have had vinyl reprints come out like CRAZY in the last few years, but Grimey's didn't have much for any of them. It's not something that totally kills this place for me, but I like a lot of variety in the shops I go to. If you're there looking for new release albums or reprints, this is definitely your place. Just don't expect to find many hidden gems in the packed, cramped Used section. In the end, I picked up Acts 1 and 2 from The Protomen on CD for about $20 and left very happy. Nevertheless, Grimey's is AWESOME. They had great music playing, a solid collection of new releases, and a fun, friendly atmosphere. I'll definitely be back the next time I'm in Nashville, but I'm hoping I find more of the stuff I usually look for.
label: POS

text: I know the old saying is "I'm tired of gin, I'm tired of sin, and after last night, oh boy am I tired." Sub bourbon ('The Seelbach' I believe it was called?) for gin, and that would pretty well summarize my night. Wow! My companion noted--and rightly so--that this place is bringing the drink mixology of Indianapolis to the next level. The ingredients used were fresh, meticulously measured (when's the last time you've seen bartenders using a 'jigger'?), leading to my one criticism about this lovely place: size. An 'Old Fashioned' arrived in a seriously old-fashioned serving...harkening the days when a glass of water arrived in a 6 oz. (or less) receptacle. And while the food was mighty tasty, the movie 'L.A. Story' came to mind--images of a giant plate with tiny food. The tomato terrine was a savory mouth-party, but clearly meant for one, even though it is presented in two pieces. Sharing it will leave 2 wishing for more than 1 each. The crostini was yummy (loved the rosemary oil) and the idea of the crushed walnuts, but since the crostini was toasted to the point of shattering upon the impact of the first bite, I ended up losing most of the walnuts--so if they toasted the bread a little less, or ground the walnuts more finely, I could have gotten more swept onto my taste buds. The bacon quartet (?) (don't recall it's official moniker)...well, really what more needs to be said? Can you go wrong with bacon? Let me answer that for you: no, not really. I don't recall all the varieties, but I will say, they were all adequately lip-licking good and I enjoyed the accompanying sauce smears. However, again...I was left wanting more. I've never been the type to obsess about size. I am not a fan of Cheesecake Factory portions, and I get that these are carefully crafted pieces of culinary art, but in this case, I wanted bigger. And I wanted more. I will be back, undoubtedly, because I loved it, but may not be able to share with my companions, be forewarned.

text: This established eatery should be much better than it is, because it has a lot going for it (history, location, ambience, menu and service). But management needs to stop resting on it's laurels and take a look at how they are doing business because there is a LOT of competition in New Orleans and this place is currently not up to par. The dining room is not large and it should be easily packed each night, even during the summer, but the night we went we were one of 3 couples that were there between the hours of 6pm and 8pm. Odd, but there are several reasons why. First: there is no menu posted on the door, nor is there any indication to people walking by that this is a 6-course prix-fixe establishment. While we dined we watched MANY strollers-by look for a posted menu, peek in, see what were only a few diners inside (it must have looked creepy, and sad), and walk away. Even our busser was surprised at how empty it was. The few brave souls who did walk inside to ask the waitstaff questions about the menu opted to go elsewhere because we didn't see them come in. Suggestion: post outside the general prix-fixe roadmap (i.e. Your Complete Dining Experience Awaits You Inside, featuring Appetizer, Salad, Soup, Entree, Dessert and Coffee, all for just $48 per person). It would be helpful, too, if the management would decide on a SINGLE PRICE for the menu -- it differs based on the entree you order which, I feel, is silly. Make it EASY and INVITING for your potential customers to come in -- most want a general outline of their experience as well as how much the food will cost. (P.S. As other Yelpers have stated, "Coffee" is NOT a course! Coffee can and should be offered with dessert, but it should not receive it's own course billing!) Second: yes, this place is old and historic and lots and lots of people have eaten here, but I think it's time the photos of Judge Judy, Regis Philbin and Debby Boone be taken off the walls (not that I have anything against those celebrities -- I don't -- but it just screams "I am a dated restaurant" to the world. Also, there is a glass-enclosed "museum" of little spirit bottles high along one wall, much like a young man collects and displays aluminum cans and/or beer bottles in a bedroom. I'm sorry, but this is not art, and also makes the dining room seem tacky. Please take down the photos and bottles and paint the room a rich, dark color to go with the wood-work and lighting; more people might like the looks from outside and actually come in. This place has huge potential to be a romantic, classy environment and it would be so easy to make these changes! If the little bottles and photos are important the history of the restaurant I suggest they be moved to the bar area. Three: when we walked in this place smelled, well, old. Not that it smelled like sewage or anything but walking into this type of place one SHOULD encounter incredible, inviting aromas. It just smelled like an older building that was holding onto the food and weather odors of several generations. So, I have awarded 2 stars. One is for the wait-staff (who, based on the photos on the walls, have been working there a long time). They are extremely professional and respectful to their patrons. The other is for the Creamed Corn Soup, which was fresh and creative and such a nice change of pace after seeing Gumbo and Turtle Soup on every menu. This course was by far my favorite of the meal, and I wish I had asked how to make it at home. I also award a 1/2 star to the Beef Brisket, which was tender and delicious (I wish we could award 1/2 stars on Yelp, because I would do so in this case). I am rooting for Tujaques and really want it to be better; it has the potential to be quite the hotspot (the stand-up bar located on the corner of the property is unusual and, with just a few modern updates should be packed as well). If someone would please just take the time (and money) to make just a few updates this long-standing establishment would be more appealing to today's educated diners.

The staff is pleasant, the grounds are very clean, the animals appear to be well taken care of, and the playground is amazing - you could spend an hour or two just playing in the playground! text: If you're thinking, "what the hell was Justin doing at a bar in St. Louis?" I can promise you I was wondering the same damn thing. Flying back to Los Angeles from Chicago after Christmas had me connecting through St. Louis which I'm sure would have been fantastic except for the gazillion fucking people who were bumped off flights with me due to bad weather around the country. No better way to wrap up holiday times than a 24 hour stint in St Louis, that's what I always (sarcastically) say. So I did what any self respecting lush does: booked a hotel room, dropped off my shit, and immediately found the closest bar to drink down the hyper-irritation I had from sitting in an airport for 15 hours. Not just any airport, but the St Louis airport where two separate restaurants tried to argue with me that chicken stock was in fact vegetarian so needless to say I didn't eat anything other than a bag of chips all day. My hotel told me about Yesterday's and I figured why not, I certainly wasn't going to sit on my ass in the hotel room, drinks and food sounded spot on. End result? Yesterday's was... interesting, in a good way. It's pretty much what I would expect for a rural Midwest bar; greasy bar food, cheap drinks, music that hurt my ears, and very friendly people. I sat at this spot for maybe an hour and a half and the bartender was outgoing and chatty, keeping me company. The regulars told me all about where to get the best food while in town and then talked football with me. All in all I've had plenty of bar visits far worse than this one. I have to say thank you, they made my layover a lot less painful. I got a little buzz, had a little conversation, and then headed back to my room to completely destroy a cheeseless pizza from Dominos. Like completely and utterly destroyed it, within 3 minutes. I have to say for being on the completely opposite side of the country from where I live, Yesterday's did a pretty good job of making me feel at home. I'll take good conversation with chill people over a pompous lounge or club any day of the week.

They said their Wonton soup to be good, but then again, how can you possibly mess up Wonton soup? The final member of our party had some sushi. Overall, it seems that this place tries is trying to cater to too many tastes (large menu, varied tastes) at the same time, but they stretch themselves too thin and fail at all of them (this have all the typical dishes of a Chinese restaurant, but not even the most basic a dishes are any good). The owners should put more work on improving the quality of their dishes than the quantity of their selection. text: Ok...so I live in the neighborhood, and have friends who absolutely LOVE this place. I'm rarely in the mood for music so loud I can't hear the person next to me, but I've been a few times, because I enjoy the outdoor seating and the opportunity to people watch. The food is average, the service is pretty sub-par (whoever said it seems like the entire staff is nursing a collective PBR-induced hangover hit the nail on the head). But the bar at PYT can be a fun spot, if you happen to walk in on a day when it's not overflowing with hipster wannabes who have taken the day off from Sea Isle to guzzle beer and fist pump in their neon sunglasses (circa 1987). I've actually had some borderline nice experiences at the bar at PYT. The DJs they have are actually very talented, and I love the eclectic mix of 80s music, old school hip-hop, and current stuff; it's the volume thing that bothers me most of the time. There are a few bartenders who are warm and friendly (two females in particular, whose names I can't remember, but one has a great partial sleeve on one arm), but for the most part, the staff (male bartenders in particular) give off a vibe that they really couldn't care less about their customers. Having worked in the industry, this attitude really pisses me off. I couldn't figure out how PYT's employees got away with ignoring their customers on such a regular basis, until the last time I went in, with some out of town guests. As we were settling our tabs (which were much higher than we expected them to be), I happened to glance at the chalkboard behind the bar, which lists the beers and the daily specials. There, in rather small, handwritten print, it said, "20% gratuity added to all bills." Never before had I noticed this "sign," and never before (in my 5 or 6 times there) had a server or bartender informed me of this policy. I'm not even sure if this policy is legal. I mean...sure, we all expect the 18% gratuity added to checks when we go out w/ parties of 6 or more. But three people, sitting at a half-empty bar on a Saturday afternoon, drinking beers and watching the Phils game??? Our bartender said something to the effect of, "Oh, wow. I really didn't think you guys drank that much!" when she gave us our tabs, and asked us to check and make sure she hadn't accidentally charged us twice for anything (since we had two tabs going). Had she not said this, I wouldn't have noticed the 20% gratuity that had been added. So I'm not sure if she was suggesting we look at it, as a way of getting us to stumble upon the automatic gratuity, or if she was genuinely worried she had overcharged us. But the bottom line is, she (and every other server/bartender there) should have just come out and said, "Hey, not sure if you noticed the tiny little chalk-written note on the beer board, but there's an automatic 20% gratuity added to every bill." Naturally, I had already added a 20% tip to my bill (on TOP of the 20% they had already charged), but I hadn't given it back to her yet. So I tossed the first copy into my purse, and recalculated on the 2nd copy. Honestly...I don't know if this is illegal, but it certainly seems unethical, and it's DEFINITELY offensive, especially to a person who tips extremely well on a regular basis. And, honestly, the service at PYT is among the worst I've ever had. They're slow, they're not friendly, and they act like they don't give a sh*t. Which they probably don't, since they get 20% regardless. If you're looking for a laidback time at a bar and you don't care if it takes half an hour to get each of your drinks...give it a try. And try a pickleback shot while you're there. They make their own pickles in-house, and the pickle juice is delicious. But BEWARE of the automatic 20% gratuity.

Very nicely decorated lobby with neat & eclectic decor (roller skate at front desk, bike at window, blueprints book & paper tower at entrance, etc.). Friendly staff. Plenty of elevators. Clean rooms with modern decor. Cute carpets in rooms. Plenty of mirrors, including the make up one & full length one. Comfortable bed & lots of pillows. Good size flat screen TV. Plenty of lighting, including a light in the shower which many hotels lack. A decent sized fitness room. And a great complimentary wine hour (5:00-6:00 PM)! We didn't get to do this cause of time constraints but they let you borrow bikes, a helmet & lock. My only complaint was it took 20 minutes to get the car from the valet when my co-worker & I had to get to a work site. So we arrived 30 minutes late.

text: I was so hoping for this place to be amazing. We have been wanting a local Italian place to frequent near our house since we moved to south Reno. Saddly, this won't be the place. The location is cool, on longly next to Cafe de Thai. It's 2 story. We weren't sure what to do when we walked in though. No one was in the small room, and the tables were all vacant. We walked up stairs and again no one was there. We turned around to go back down and were greeted in the stairwell by 2 people that work there. Both were very nice, it was early so we got to pick wherever we wanted to sit. I'm giving one star for the cool building lay out, and one star for the service (if I were doing this review based only on service it would be 5 stars). Our server was friendly, knowledgable and extremely willing to work with my dairy free requests. Hubby and I both started out with the minestrone soup. It was luke warm, and full of garlic. Now I love garlic. But that is all I could taste. For the entrees my husband ordered the spaghetti marinara with sausage. Again, all you can taste is garlic. The noodles were slightly under cooked, and the marinara was extrememly sweet. The sausage was good. I ordered the puttanesca. It was supposed to be rich in olive and caper flavor, which I LOVE. Again all I could taste? You guessed it! Garlic. It did end on a happy note though, the bill was only $26. Oh and another disapointment is that you have to exit the restaurant to use the bathroom that they share with Cafe de Thai.
label: NEG

text: Neveria La Vallesana has won my heart, or at least my tummy. I will admit, when we were first greeted and seated, I was grumbling. No chips and salsa brought to the table and no liquor license, which meant no Margarita. How do they expect me to eat Mexican food without chips and liquid refreshment? To my surprise I enjoyed my street tacos much more, because I had not filled myself up with countless chips and a boozy drink. The SO was in the mood to make his "world famous" tamales so we made a trip down to Cherokee for his special ingredients. We knew not to grocery shop on an empty stomach, so we stopped in Neveria La Vallesana. We each had three street tacos and a side of beans. I choose, shredded pork, chicken and grilled steak. All three were flavorful, but next time and there will be a next time I will be ordering all three chicken. Yes, the chicken was that flavorful. The service was friendly and with the good food, this will be one of my regular haunts for Mexican food. Can't wait for them to get a liquor license.

text: I contacted this company based on their three 5-star reviews on Yelp (two of which have since been filtered, interestingly enough) to inquire about management services for our Tucson home. I followed up with them after waiting the 5 days, and they claimed that each of two guys thought that the other one had responded to me. They finally went to view the property with my husband, and the guy kept telling him "When I spoke to your mother on the phone..." (referring to me, his wife - not only had I told him that he would be meeting my husband, but I'm in my 20s, and I sound like I'm about 12 on the phone...). He clearly was confusing us with someone else. After viewing the home, we received no further response from them for nearly 2 weeks. I sent them an email (copying all 3 gentlemen I had been emailing with previously) asking how soon they could get the property listed. When I didn't hear from them for 2 days, I emailed again, asking them to confirm that we should seek out a different management service. They finally wrote back, claiming that they never received my email, and that they feel they are "too busy" to take on our property right now. While I appreciate them telling me that they are "too busy" to manage our property, they really should have told us that up front, or as soon as they realized it - not several weeks later when we were counting on using them. It's also really uncool to claim that nobody received my email, when I had copied the 3 of them on it, as well as my husband, and my husband received it (and I received no undeliverable message). Now I have to search for a new property management company and we're at the point where we need the property rented out now. I have to wonder where their 5-star reviews came from... The only saving grace is that I didn't find out how bad they are at communication AFTER entering an agreement with them!
