text: We go to the Royal Alberta Museum with our daughter (and soon - our son who will be born next month) at least once a year. I have to admit we usually go on Family Day when it's free (the 3rd week in February). I'm pretty sure we usually go on the busiest day of the year & we always enjoy it immensely! There is a good variety of things to look at from fossils and bugs to Aboriginal culture including teepees that children can explore. I really appreciate how the children's exhibit changes throughout the year - we've seen lego exhibits and this past one was a Robert Munsch exhibit - AWESOME! I don't know if they always have tables set up with various professionals doing "show and tell" but on Family Day the 2nd floor is filled with tables of things - alive (bugs, fish tanks, etc.) and dead (fossils, animal furs) to look at and explore along with speakers/students/profs to talk about the items. They have a cafe if you need to get a little bite to eat and a cute little souvenier store that we always manager to find something to buy in. I look forward to discovering what the new exhibits will be next time!

text: I'm from Dubai and Toronto, been to some of the finest restaurants in both cities, but I must say that d'Lish is by far one of the best I've been to! On a recent visit to Alberta, escaping my life and the hustle n bustle of To, I decided to visit a friend of mine in Edmonton. The moment I landed I felt like royalty...my friend's gorgous condo which seemed more like a stylish loft/town home, manis and pedis in the afternoon, followed by a faboulous dinner at this lovely restaurant! We were a group of 6, and we started off by wine and some nibbles. Gourmet popcorn...what an ingenious idea!! There were 2 types, truffled oil and maple bacon...i preferred the former but enjoyed the sweetness of the latter..I wish I knew how they did this and I'd have movie nights at home in complete bliss! So now with regards to the food, 4 of us went for the surprise 10 course meal..and boy were we surprised...shocked that it was SOOO d'Lish-ous! We had a wide variety of different textures, flavours, colours..exactly how a meal should me...innovative creations like Shrimp with a sauce in shot glasses, scallops, mushroom crepes, turkey dinner (bread, chutney and turkey balls), beef ribs in mustard sauce...simply DIVINE! all sorts of other goodies too..and portions were terrific! The dessert was tiny, but oh so good..truffled chocolate in some sort of dreamy rasberry coulis sauce garnished with nuts. At that point we didn't mind the smaller dessert as we were so full with everything else. My friend who decided to go with an individual entree had the veggie flatbread pizza...which I tried a little...also baked to perfection. We were thoroughly impressed by the friendly service, the mouth watering food, the elegant decor...maybe I'm in love with this restaurant because I'm not from Edmonton and I know I can't visit it that much (we always want what we can't have!) but I have to say...FABULOUS venue..whether you're on a date, a birthday dinner, or simply dining solo , D'lish is the best choice! text: Every year I plan our small company holiday dinner and chose a restaurant that I think will provide a fun atmosphere for my staff and their spouses to enjoy an evening together. I thought that was odd, so I called the restaurant directly and easily made a reservation for 8 over the phone. Why not make all your available tables available on Open Table? When making the reservation, the staff asked if it was a special occasion. I told them it was my company holiday party and that I would appreciate a nice table where our entire group could talk and be comfortable. Sure, no problem is was told. In the week leading up to the reservation, I received two calls to confirm the reservation. Each time, I confirmed for 8 people and they also asked the "special occasion" question again, to which I told them that it as our holiday party and asked for a table where we could all talk. I took one look and knew that there was no way 8 adults were cramming into a booth, with a small table attached. The hostess says, 6 people can easily sit here. I agreed, but reminded her that we had a party of 8, which seemed to be news to her. After a coupe minutes of confusion, another hostess/manager comes to me and asks me to follow her to another table shed thinks might work. I follow her and she shows me a table set for six. I remind her again that we have 8 and she looks at me like I'm crazy for not considering cramming 8 people into this table. After some back and forth, it comes down to that we can have the booth in the corner, the table set for six or leave. I reluctantly agree to squeeze us into the corner booth and half of us sink into the booth seats while the other half tower above us in chairs. There is something not right about making a grown man ask three of his co-workers to "slide out" of the booth so he can take a piss. (Am I alone here?) To management's credit, they did send a fried mozzarella app and some garlic bread to the table for our inconvenience. Once the food started to arrive, we were also disappointed. Still good, but nothing to write home about. Our waitress was very nice and seemed to be trying to make up for the seating fiasco, which I appreciate. Overall, the meal was not worth the aggravation of the table issue. If you are going to ask a customer three times if they are celebrating a special occasion, you better do something with the info they give you. text: It has a very interesting decor and is a unique building, so this might be a good place to have a drink, but I'm not sure I would return to dine here. It has a unique flavor on the back end, which I can only guess was the rum, and was easy to drink. I would definitely recommend these. Appetizers: Trying to decide between Billy Goat Chips & Dip, White Bean & Artichoke Brulee, and Bacon Wrapped Dates ($6.95, see picture), we asked the server for a recommendation. He answered quickly with the dates, and we were not disappointed. These were a unique blend of salty and sweet that worked and came with a nice dipping sauce. Plate of Food: I would not get this. My friend ordered the Plate of Food. She received 2 chili dogs (see picture). Nothing else with it, no sides or veggies, just 2 hot dogs in buns covered in chili, cheese, and bacon bits for $9.95. Not exactly the type of meal most females want for a Saturday night dinner at 7pm for $9.95. Even if they tasted ok, $9.95 is pricey for 2 chili dogs. We happened to arrive just after 2 large tables had ordered and figured the kitchen/chef was so busy with their order, that's why the Plate of Food at the moment was chili dogs, because it was easy to do. Cajun Salmon ($11.95, see picture): The salmon was very good in a tasty sauce with a tiny bit of heat. I can't usually handle spicy, but this was pretty good. The red beans and rice, however, was a whole other story. I took one bite and - what I'm guessing was - the cayenne on the rice was all I could taste for 1/2 the meal. It was soooo spicy hot, I could not touch the rice the rest of the meal. The green beans seemed raw. At first, I thought they were just steamed, but then I tasted the bitterness of the raw bean and noticed they were overly crunchy. I know some people eat green beans raw, but it's just not what I was expecting to come with the salmon.

text: So a bunch of my guy friends have been raving nonstop about the lasagna and pizza here so when they invited me to check it out with them, I couldn't say no. The pizzas are a bit expensive, but they are huge, fresh, delicious, and worth it. They will gladly make you a pizza half & half with the variety of toppings offered including artichokes (yum!) and spinach and all the regular meats. I wasn't able to try any of their pastas or other dishes but I've heard great things about them. But, let me tell you, do not come here on an empty stomach expecting to order, get your food, and get out. There is a wait in line and a wait for the food. A long wait in anticipation for the food. A wait so long that every 5 minutes you're second-guessing whether or not they've forgotten your order. You'll play mind tricks on yourself, asking yourself over and over again, "Did she really hear my order? Did I give her my name? Did someone take our pizza? Did those guys come before us or after us? How come they got their food first? Will they run out of dough? Are they closing shop?" That being said, however, they won't forget your order. I was a little concerned at first because we had to repeat our order twice; I almost got the impression that we were bothering her or troubling her by taking our order. But our pizza came out perfectly fine. Although, it took what seemed like an hour before it came out. And they don't forget you. We had been waiting there for a while (it made for a good time of catching up with old friends) and randomly, the lady from behind the counter motioned to my friend. No words, no yelling, just a simple head gesture, beckoning him to come forward. Silence. She hands him a plate of baked dough doused in some olive oil, fresh from the oven. The dough probably comes from leftovers from rolling pizzas, but boy did it whet our appetites. It was deliciously fresh and irresistible. I've always wanted to act in a sitcom, and something about this place reminds me of the Soup Nazi in Seinfeld. Except it's the pizza Nazi. There aren't many wall decorations, just your average cafeteria-style small beginnings. No waiters or waitresses serving you on hand and feet. No one to bus your table for you or refill your Coke. And your regular table conversations will be interrupted by some backstage yelling between the workers or maybe at a customer. You might get a curt or rude word here or there--but it's all part of the experience. Don't come in a rush or with a naive spirit--this is New York Pizza we're talking about...don't expect that Southern hospitality.

text: Chris McMillan. On a Sunday night. OH MY GOD. On this last trip to New Orleans for a conference, I knew I only had limited time to do the cocktail rounds, and sadly couldn't make it out to Bar UnCommon on a Sunday night. At first, my partner and I thought we were in the wrong place- it's right in the middle of the lobby, and looks like a totally tacky "modernist" hotel bar that was trying way too hard (like the rest of the Pere Marquette, it's plagued by the "W disease" of bad modernist interpretations.) Imagine my total shock to see at the near-empty bar Chris McMillan himself, slinging vodka cranberries and Blue Moons to the clueless other patrons. I tried not to be a fangirl but I couldn't help it. Once he figured out my partner and I actually came for one of his cocktails, he was super sweet and made us cocktails based on our conversations-- a Campari mojito for him, a "big girl Manhattan" with Bookers and later, a French Pearl, for me. All of which were, of course, amazing. He also gave us some fascinating history of liquors like absinthe and bitters, and I only wish we had more time to stay and chat. Thank you to the other bartender at UnCommon that graduated college this past weekend, needing Chris to fill in-- if it weren't for you, we never would've had to chance to meet him that night! You could tell the rest of tourists at the bar were annoyed he was taking so long with our drinks, but screw them! If you're here asking for a Michelob, you'll just have to wait!

text: I'm trying to find an excellent Chinese take-out place in the Palm Harbor area, and haven't had much success. So I'm working my way through all the Yelp listings I haven't tried yet. I stopped in for supper at China Taste with a family member after receiving a flyer on my doorstep from them. China Taste is located in the Boot Ranch shopping center between Target and Publix. The dining room has a few tables available for eating-in, and the room was clean and neat. Order taking was prompt, and the food arrived quickly. I ordered a chicken & shrimp with broccoli special, and switched the pork fried rice to chicken, and my guest ordered a standard chicken and broccoli combo meal. I added egg roll and wonton soup, and my guest's combo came with egg roll. As for the food, I found it uninspiring. In other cities I usually find it hard to be disappointed with Chinese take-out food. I'm not sure why, but I've found very few really good places in the Clearwater/Palm Harbor area, with the average place here below most other cities I've lived/spent time in. I say all of that to emphasize my expectations here for Chinese take-out are pretty low. But China Taste failed to meet even these lowered expectations. I found the wonton soup flavorful, but nothing remarkable. The egg roll was a bit overdone, and had very little flavor. The chicken fried rice was bland and lacked any significant flavors or seasonings. On balance, the chicken & shrimp and broccoli flavors were a bit better and well-cooked, but nothing to rave about. As for value, the portions for everything were ample, and I was only able to eat about half of my meal. When the food is great, it's a bonus to take home leftovers. When the food is not so great and the leftovers got thrown away, it simply makes the meal more expensive. I won't be going back to China Taste, and that was echoed by my guest. My scores, on my "Chinese-take-out" scale : Atmosphere: 3 Service: 4 Food: 2 Value: 2 I'm moving on my next target, Big Bok Choy Bistro on Tampa Rd. in Oldsmar.
label: NEG

text: I bought a 4 person groupon for a 3-course menu, and dined here with my foodie family (incl. 2 teens) for an earlyish Sunday dinner. Overall, i have to say it was a "meh, with potential"... I wish i could give it a **+ . The baguettes and EVO were very good. The first course- a pulsed (more substantial than puréed) green & red gazpacho-was not only beautiful looking but deliciouswith fabulous fresh flavors, topped with a dollop of basil gelato that added a creamy touch of sweetness. (5*). The second course offered a choice of 4 pasta dishes. We chose the spinach manicotti and the artichoke risotto. The manicotti was 3 homemade, delicate pasta tubes lightly filled with ricotta cheese, served with a flavorful tomato squash ratatouille-like sauce... The fresh pasta was wonderful, but the chunkiness of the squash did not pair well with the delicate pasta texture, IMO. (2 1/2*). The risotto was over salted and underdone, and the fresh artichokes were not entirely tender (pointy leaves left on), which is too bad b/c the flavors and textures could have been great. (2*). The entrees we tried were also a mixed bag. DH had the "baseball cut" steak, which was Outstanding...a home run (5*). DD1 and I both had the fish (sea bass), pan seared with thinly sliced fresh truffle on top, sitting on puréed beets and cornmeal coated/fried tomato slices. This could have been another great dish, but the fish was under /un-seasoned (I never ask for salt, but did for this), and the tomatoes and cornmeal were mushy. I loved the fresh truffle, but some truffle salt was needed. The pureed beets (which I loved alone) did not add anything except beautiful red color, to the blandness of the (albeit very fresh) fish or the mushy cornmeal coated tomatoes. (2*). DD2 had the roasted eggplant caponata stack....a dish with so much potential, that was simply disappointing. The eggplant was not completely cooked (undercooked eggplant is like eating a dry sponge)- especially disappointing since we were the only diners at the time, but the sauce was otherwise very tasty. We didn't have time for dessert. I think there are some kinks to work out with the menu, while some of the dishes are already clear hits.

text: This was my first time running the Rock 'n Roll Mardi Gras half marathon. I really enjoyed the experience. The course was nice and flat, except for all the pot holes. The health and fitness expo was huge! I think it has to be the biggest one I've been to for a Rock 'n Roll run (I've done RnR San Jose, RnR Las Vegas and RnR Mardi Gras). I really liked the design for the tech-t. It wasn't the typical boring RnR design they usually have. I wonder if it is because this was the inaugural RnR Mardi Gras run? I thought maybe they should have done separate t-shirt colors too, like they did for the inaugural Las Vegas RnR run, but oh well. We purchased the pass for the shuttle ride ($20 for one car, but good for up to four people on the shuttle) to the start from the college which is right next to the park where the run finishes. It was very convenient and well worth it. When we arrived at the start area, they already had booths set up with volunteers handing out water and energy bars! They even had port-o-potties next to each starting corale. Talk about thinking ahead and being organized! It was quite cold in the morning standing around, stretching and waiting for the run to start. It was nice to see that quite a few people wore costumes for the run. Overall it was a great event and they actually had a band that I wanted to stay around to listen to after the run.

text: 4.5 stars for SideBern's. It's hard to top the original Bern's in terms of service, food quality and value for what you're getting, and SideBern's wisely doesn't even try. Instead, they opt for a more contemporary fusion menu which rotates out based on the availability of local ingredients. Very similar to the Refinery, except I think SB nails the ambiance a lot better. We spent two hours at the restaurant during our dining experience and it was a very comfortable place to do it. This was an anniversary dinner for my wife and I, so I tried to make it a little more special by ordering a bottle of champagne when I made the reservations. The staff on the phone was very accommodating with helping me pick out a good choice. Be prepared for a little sticker shock even for aged liquor, but I assure you it's well worth it. Their beer selection is also very impressive and looks as if the selections were hand picked to go along with the food being presented. The rest of the wait staff were very friendly and even stopped by our table to wish us a happy anniversary. Even better than booze, they also have an entire vegetarian menu which rotates out along with their normal menu. They don't scale back on it at all either, so there are plenty of choices. My wife and I went with the $55per person tasting, which consisted of 6 courses and a little pre-appetizer course. Since there was so much food flying around I won't fill up this review with every little dish, but suffice to say there was ample variety. Highlights include an almond vichysoise with goat cheese which left us aching for more, oregano scened tofu with some amazing chick pea puree that I will never be able to duplicate, polenta that gives mac and cheese a run for its money with wild mushrooms, and a macadamia nut bread pudding that somehow filled the remaining gaps left in my stomach. To me, SideBerns is the epitome of a good romantic restaurant. While food plays a central role, it's really about the whole experience. The wait staff are just there to aid and facilitate conversation between you and your loved one. The food, just another topic of conversation and something you get to share. And the champagne is there to make you seem just the slightest bit more insightful and witty. I don't say any of that to devalue the food, staff, or decor, but to pay it a very high compliment. Check it out for your next special occasion!

So your left eating slightly warm or cold amounts of red sauce. Not appealing. It is a sweet red sauce and the sweetness can overpower your taste buds. Less sauce would present a better balance of sweet and savory. But if sweet is your thing, you'll probably like this pizza. The crust was thin and made with corn meal. It is flavorful, but again, over-powered by not only the sweet sauce, but the weight of the sauce itself. The inner part of the pizza falls apart when you lift the slice. Go with slightly less sauce. Overall, a good pizza. The white pizza was good as well. You pick up the garlic and salt and it all blends well with the crust. The broccoli did not taste fresh, rather tasted as if it were frozen, or over cooked. I can't be certain. Having read rave reviews about Penny's, I was a little disappointed. I do think they have solid pies but I have had far better. Penny's does not deliver and there is no dining area, take-out only. They do have soda's available. The hours are very limited, Thursday - Sunday from 3-9pm. The prices are more than reasonable. You would think a pizza only shop, so focused on a few items would be a stand-out. It is tasteful but not really unique. Although I can understand the higher ratings based on limited selection in this area. Put Penny's in downtown Philly or anywhere in NYC, and well, it just wouldn't fare well. I think the Pottstown/Limerick area has fairly low standards so it's not hard to impress people. I agree with the first reviewer, Penny's has a legacy following but I question their taste buds. When I was picking up my order, I was the only person out of 5 that was under 60. I'm just saying... text: Oh...a tiny breakfast. How quaint. After reading reviews extolling the virtues of Chhaya, I was anxious to witness this culinary righteousness for myself. My Lady and I agreed to blow off our usual brunch favourtites, and instead head over to E. Passyunk Street. We walked into a dining room which was slightly smaller than our living room, albeit tidy. We were immediately informed that there is no table service on the weekdays, lest we ask for more than we are entitled to. We sat down and perused le menu. Waffles seemed to be the speciality of the house, so we decided to try them. My CD sized waffle arrived at my table unaccompanied by any of the usual suspects...not even a lowly garnish. Lady Mary's breaky looked similarly lonely, but at least we each had a non-refillable $4 cup of coffee to keep our waffles company. The flavour wasn't at all bad, however. The sausage gravy was acceptably authentic (on mine), and nutella was used in a reserved judicious manner (on the other). The main problem is that the portion wasn't even close to meal sized. I felt like I was being punished for some unknown transgression. No table service for you Urqhart!!! And I hope you like your waffles extra small boy!!!!! MUAHHAAA!!! We ate silently as stroller after stroller bumped into our table. I must admit, I didn't at all agree with the rave reviews I read here; quite the contrary. Beau Monde is to Chhaya as Miles Davis is to Kenny G. As an aside, we've noticed most of the restaurants in the Passyunk square follow a bit of a motif. State Side, Plenty, Chhaya, Cantina, Birra...all entirely too hip for your own good. Owners need to do two things: 1. Go to a good pub in Europe (that's the hard one), and 2. go around the corner to Carmen's Country Kitchen. It's elevated, with a good deal less 'la-de-da', and one leaves feeling with the satisfaction of just having eaten a holiday meal. I don't care that all the restaurants in the square have artisan light bulbs. I don't care that the portions are stylishly lilliputian . I don't care that the napkins are made from recycled grocery bags. I truly, truly, with all my heart, don't care. I just want quality food (and enough to fill me up), sometimes a decent pint, at a good price. I'm putting the Passyunk Square on my no fly zone for the foreseeable future. Off to greener pastures.

text: One day during a recent trip to Nashville, Mr. Babypants passed out in his seat and lunch had to be had in the car. Luckily we were close by Five Points, a small commercial district that splinters off of Gallatin Pike in East Nashville, so I popped into Five Points Pizza and ordered slices. I didn't take in much of the interior design other than it fits into that increasingly common contemporary-and-sleek-but-a-little-bit-rustic-and-industrial milieu. All I remember is that I immediately felt like I made the right decision. I bypassed the greeter and went straight to the bar to order carryout. Prosciutto and basil and straight pepperoni slices were the most appealing on that day's lineup and 10 minutes later they were ready. text: If Occupy Philly had a sponsor, I like to think Underdogs would be it. It's a place where revolutionary spirit drapes the walls with its raised, clenched fist mural; the kind of artwork that would be welcoming to a group that, say, might want to overthrow the Fed and return to the gold standard. But as far as I can tell, Underdogs is less concerned with Ben Bernanke and more focused on putting out great hot dogs. The buns are not the flimsy 4th of July cookout ones you snag off a grocery store shelf. Sturdy, crackly sides are just dense and chewy enough to make you appreciate the quality rolls without any unnecessary padding. A proper meat/toppings to bread ratio is paramount and they've got it down. The Special ($3.50), with pepper hash and russian dressing, probably pairs nicely with 6-8 lagers and is a late night craving waiting to happen. The Chihuahua ($4.50) was my only foray into the sausages and the queso blanco adds a nice, needed smooth finish to play against the sharp spices of chorizo. The salty peanut taste of the My Thai ($4) dog marries well with the cool, crispy papaya slaw, but I only want peanut sauce with chicken and some kind of noodle. The fries ($2.25/reg) stand up on their own merit. Unless a better writer shows up to finish this review I'll lazily tell you to think of Five Guys fries, greasy paper bag and all. But stay away from the ketchup when you peel back your greasy bag of spuds. Utah sauce is another weird cult-ish thing to come out of Utah, but this one is actually worth following blindly. Ketchup, mayo, and pickle juice--stop, get that look off your face--forms a surprisingly addicting condiment. It's a fairly smooth concoction before the pickle juice kicks your palate with just a bit of brine. There was nothing wrong with the chocolate cayenne mole--nice heat and all--I just didn't think it matched up well with the spuds. The curry is good, too, and lacks heat if you shy away from it typically. First dipping sauce is free, second is 25 cents. Get at least two.

text: Hmm, can one really be a fan of anything dentist-related? Well, I guess I can safely say that they keep my teeth happy, so in that regard, I guess I am indeed a fan! I have been going to this dentist (Dr. Wong specifically) for the better part of 10 years now. Initially, I was a little alarmed at the number of diagnosed cavities that I was having. So I went to another dentist just to check that I was being treated fairly and honestly. And sure enough, I had cavities--I blame the Tucson water! So I returned with peace of mind to Dr. Wong. In all those years, I've had 6-month check-ups and cleanings, cavities filled, fillings replaced, and a crown to replace a broken tooth. All this was done in the office and to my satisfaction. The only referral I ever needed was to have my 4 wisdom teeth removed. He sent me to an oral surgeon who was more than competent for that. The only issue I really have is that they like to take x-rays once per year. I find that to be a little too often. Fortunately, you can opt out of them. The staff have pretty much stayed the same over the 10 years--a sign of a boss who cares for his business. It's a small office on 5th St. It has a definite family feel to it. I like that. The dental technicians are wonderful, cheerful, and fairly good about how aggressively they clean your teeth. I like that too. Lastly, they take a wide variety of insurance. I know they honor MetLife. Calling to see if they accept your plan before visiting is always good planning though. Lastly, every 6-month checkup includes a new toothbrush, a travel-sized floss container, and a travel-sized tube of toothpaste. All perfect for those trips where you have to pack light!

text: Can I start by saying that I think it's a little weird to be reviewing a road? We took what will become the first of many Trace trips the other weekend. We admired views from the lookout points, we read up on Trace history at the points of interest, we hiked, we sat at picnic tables to enjoy snacks and frosty beverages, we took a thousand pictures... Such an awesome day. Points of interest are well marked, so you really don't have to know what you're looking for to find things to do. We had no agenda besides restaurants we wanted to try, we just started driving and stopped whenever we saw something interesting. Most of the stops were completely empty, so we felt like we had the whole Trace pretty much to ourselves. You'd see another couple or family every once and a while, but we just made them our photographers so that my stretched arm wasn't in every picture we took when there was a pretty attraction like Jackson Falls. Food wise, we stopped in Leiper's fork at Puckett's for lunch on the way out of town (and spent time wandering around there too) and hit up Papa Boudreaux's in Santa Fe for dinner on the way back. text: In Chicago, my favorite pizza place (for deep dish pizza anyway) is Lou Malnati's. Pi reminds me of it in a lot of ways -- there are differences, but it's the closest thing to that that I've found here. I've had the gluten-free pizza here too and it's pretty good. One thing that's been great about St Louis is that the cost of living is less than in Chicago. Often I find myself spending a lot less at restaurants, in particular. I don't find that that extends to pizza places, though. I'm not sure why that is; maybe it's just all of the bread and other suppliers we have in such close proximity up there. But Pi's pizzas just costs a decent amount more than I would expect. I think they're worth the money in the end, but it prevents it from being a regular spot for me. What's difficult about Chicago is that there's a million pizza places, but everyone outside of the city seems to assume all we eat is pan pizza or stuffed pizza (ala Giordanos -- or Blackthorn's here). The most common pizza everyone gets in Chicago (hell, I'd say 90% of the time in my experience) is a thicker dough, thin crust pizza with a pretty dense layer of mozarella. I have yet to find a place out here that does that the same.

I do like the large, plump shrimp they use at Verti Marte, but I am such a sucker for the bread at Parkway. My catfish was good, but I was pleasantly surprised by the pastrami. I never would have thought to order a pastrami po boy on my own, but now that I've tried it and liked it, I might get it in the future. Z seemed to enjoy his surf & turf. I tried the roast beef from his sandwich. It was good, but like I said in another po boy review, I don't think I am a fan of the roast beef po boy. text: I always enjoy McCabe. My favorite is the catfish basket. It's not the healthiest option, but boy, is it tasty! The batter is fresh and not too heavy--and the fish kind of melts out of it. text: Our lunch here started off on a positive note: we got a nice table by a window, it was quiet (the deeper meaning of this, a lack of customers, was not initially apparent), and Mr. Ponytailed Waiter was friendly and seemed attentive. I had the salmon salad: the fish, avocado and dressing were tasty, but as I dug deeper into the salad greens, I kept finding black, rotting pieces. Mr. Ponytail, who had been buzzing around before we started eating, was suddenly absent. When he did come by, I explained that much of the greens in my salad were past their prime, and I even showed him some of the gooey, decaying leaves. He looked at me with the same patronizing gaze my mother did when I was eight years old and told her I saw ghosts in our house. He said something like, "I'll let the people in the kitchen know", as if that was actually a solution to the problem, and then he took our plates away. No offer to take a few bucks off the bill, or a free dessert or drink, or even any kind of apology. Since Mr. Ponytail appeared to think I was imagining the whole thing, and that the salad was just fine, we gave him a 10% tip; he can imagine it was 20%. text: I couldn't decide where to review USAirways but chose PHL since that's there major hub and base of operations. Hopefully people looking for reviews of the airline will come by here, where there seems to be the most input. So, they kind of suck. My international flight out was cancelled. I managed to get out and fly the much nicer Aer Lingus, so that was a bonus. On the way home, once again the mysterious "mechanical failure" struck and I found myself stuck in Charlotte. As our short delay stretched out into missed connections, we all started regaling one another with tales of epic delays. Delays in Charlotte. Delays in Philadelphia. Delays international and domestic. Long, unexplained, trip-ruining delays. The extra star is for the service. It would seem that these delays and missed connections and re-routes are so normal that the staff remained friendly, calm and helpful as they slowly made arrangements to get everyone to their final destinations. They are often cheaper, but there is still a cost. Delays are more likely and the planes are old and shoddy. My international flight back, this time on US, was on a plane with *drop down video screens.* I didn't know those still existed. The toilets were so weak that they were all (and I mean all) clogged about two hours before arrival. Gross. So, I will go out of my way to avoid this airline in the future. It's not as wretched as my foresworn enemy AirTran, but it's well below par in a very competitive market.

text: this place kicked ass. i dont know how someone can go to a restaurant on opening night and bash it, especially coming from this family of restaurants. text: We went for a breakfast on the weekend. Immediately inside the door this is clearly a Bar and grill. The focus here is bar. No low tables inside to eat at. And as we did a very friendly waitress familiarized us with the place and gave us the menus. We had seen the menu online before coming down and were interested in the different benedicts that they offer. My wife immediately ordered the French Toast Benedict, I ordered the house made Corned Beef Hash, my daughter ordered a basic breakfast with eggs, bacon, potatoes and a biscuit. My son ordered up an omelet. We all loved our meals. Nothing was over $9. Did you read that? NOTHING was over $9. Oh wait, that also includes tax. Yes the prices on the menu are tax inclusive. Our food came out very quick. Hot. And very good. Nothing to complain about at all. My wife liked the French toast Bene. You could really taste the flavor of the toast under the other ingredients. Nice and light Hollandaise sauce. My house made corned beef hash was well worth getting, one point worth noting is this was wasn't a greasy mess like many corned beef hashes can be. My picky eater daughter said "I could come back and eat the eggs and biscuit for sure!" My son, a boy of few words finished his food without comment. I also ordered a Bloody Mary and at $5 it was totally worth it. I tasted the alcohol as well as the spicy goodness of the home made mix. In fact the waitress informed us that they try their best to make everything in house from scratch. Including their mixes. I guess that means we will be heading back for some other drinks to see just how far they really go. We will return for a burger. We will return for some more drinks. And we will take friends back for breakfast. One last note. Just want to note that this place proves that breakfasts can be made affordable and good and filling in Reno. This is a lesson many other places need to take note of.

After she finished keying in our order, which included five fountain drinks, she turned around to start talking to another staff member, then quickly turned back to me, gestured at the stack of cups behind the counter to the right of the register, and said "you can grab some of those for your drinks or whatever." OK then. Fine. That took place at 6:15 PM. Right after that, I checked in on Foursquare and unlocked a free smoothie special, so I went back to the register and asked for that. They brought that out in about ten minutes. Then, to make a very long story short, they eventually brought out a few salads. Then a few more. Then an entree. Then a couple more entrees. Not all in a row, but every ten minutes or so, a new dish. I overheard them talking about what else had been ordered and still needed to be prepared, and I could tell from what the guy who seemed to be the head cook was saying that he was going to prepare one order incorrectly based on what the confused girl told him, so I walked over and said "actually, that is supposed to have no tomato sauce." He was super friendly and gracious about it and thanked me for the correction because of course it's better to make it right than have to fix it. He offered a substitution of pesto which I declined. At some point after that, some guy tried to come give me the free smoothie again. I explained we already had it and he went away. Eventually all but one entree and two salads had arrived. At 7:45 PM - an hour and a half after we placed the order - the final dinner entree (the salmon) was served. Subsequent to that, the two salads were served about five minutes apart. Honestly - it was totally NOT worth the wait. I mean, I liked the food, and if it had come in a timely fashion I would have no complaints, but - this was just horrendous service. Horrendous. This place may be fine as a coffee spot, but I will NEVER again attempt a sit-down meal. I do like that they have books and magazines available - nice concept. And like I said, the food was good - but I just can't get past how outrageously bad the service was.
label: NEG

I called Old City Tans and got an appointment for later that day (a Friday). When I walked in, the owner was very nice. While she was getting my information, several regulars walked in to use the tanning beds- she greeted them all by name and set them up right away. Because this was my first time, she went through a very thorough explanation of the process and made sure I understood how to take care of the tan. I was a little shy to be in my skivvies in front of a stranger, but she kept me at ease and we chatted while she sprayed me down. I asked for just a little color- nothing too dark, and the owner was very understanding of this request. The whole process took about 30 minutes. Definitely none of this orange business. After waiting a few hours and a shower, I looked completely natural and fabulous! No one could tell I had a fake tan and the pictures from that evening are fantastic. The tan lasted just under two weeks with proper care- a great bargain for $30. I plan to go back for any events or weddings coming up; if I had more cash to spend, I would get one more often.

I said that I didn't know what that meant, and she shrugged, gave me my change and receipt and asked the next customer what she wanted to order. I was too stunned to do anything. I had a heck of a time finding outlets for my laptop that day. The place was crowded during the expected mealtimes, but it was difficult locating outlets even when the crowds went away. There just aren't as many outlets at this location as there are at other locations. I really hope the company just starts building them into the floors instead of along walls from now on. Moreover, this location was very chilly. I find many Bread Co locations to be on the cool side, but this one was legitimately blowing cold air instead of heat where I was sitting. I spoke to a cashier about it, who promised to talk to a manager. The situation improved slightly for a while, but that was because the air turned completely off, not because there was heat. Cool air soon began blowing again, and I talked to a different cashier. She also promised to figure out what was going on, but the same thing happened. I spoke to a third gentleman who came by collecting dishes, and he ran off to fiddle with the system, returning to see if things were better. Again, the cool air had stopped but there was no heat coming from the vent. Naturally, the cool air began blowing again 20 minutes later. I tried switching seats when the crowds vacated, but though I got out of the direct path of the air, I could only move within my section. I don't know if other sections had the same problem with cold vents. Unfortunately, I was forced to put on my heavy coat while eating and typing, as I still was waiting for my meeting partner to arrive after he had trouble driving in that day's very heavy winds. I'm going to have to start keeping a hoodie and fingerless gloves in my car at all times for Bread Co., Starbucks and some other chain cafes that seem to keep the thermostat set to 60 degrees year-round. Granted, I should be stockpiling clothing layers during the winter anyway for emergencies, but I'm disappointed that it's now necessary for coffeeshop tolerance.

text: Overall, I was really disappointed with my moving experience. I was really excited to hire Old City Movers. I thought with the 5 star rating, it would likely be a pretty smooth experience, and I thought it was a reasonable quote at 2 to 2 1/2 hours at $110/hr. However, when they were driving up to the alley next to my house, they swiped my mirror with the side of the moving truck. They folded in my mirror to try to prevent this, but there was not enough room and they scratched it. It's unfortunate because it was entirely preventable. I could have easily moved the car, but they didn't think to ask. They said they assumed it was someone else's car and they just thought they would try to make it around the car. The move itself went pretty smoothly. The only glitch was my couch wouldn't fit into the new apartment. Terrible experience, but I knew it was not their fault. It just didn't fit through the door, and they said the third floor apartment was too high to try to hoist a couch up. The third issue was pricing. The move took 3 hours. And also because of a miscommunication, it actually turned out to be $120/hr. The 10 small steps within my apartment counted as an extra floor, and so the price of the overall move was an extra $10/hr. So instead of $220 to 275 without tip, the price was $360. This isn't the hugest deal. I know sometimes things take longer than expected. However, if I knew, I think I would have gone with a different moving company. Tweety bird movers had a flat rate of $220. Also, I had been in touch with a smaller moving company that had a cheaper rate. At the time, I just thought it was the smart move to pay a little more for a highly recommended mover. The fourth issue came 2 days later. I kept hearing a rattle when I sat on my bed. When I investigated, I found that 3 of the 4 metal rods were never even screwed in completely. I know this because when I tried to screw them in, I had to unscrew the other side so that they would align properly. I am not sure I would have wanted to pay an extra $30 for the 15 minutes of effort it would have taken to put it together properly. However, they should have either put it together properly or at least told me they were having a problem with it. Regarding my car, they offered to go through their insurance company for the scratch on my car, but I didn't want to risk telling my car insurance company and getting an increased rate. So in the end, I just let it go. I didn't want to go through the hassle. So when I think back on my experience with old city movers, I'm fairly disappointed and mildly aggravated. I think it is very possible to have a good, smooth moving experience with old city movers, but I'm sure it can't be everyone's experience, and it certainly wasn't mine. And to be honest, I'm pretty sure I'll use a different moving company next time.

text: Exemplary service! I was all-around impressed from beginning to end. He did not make me wait until he filled the shuttle with other passengers. He carried my bags for me, drove smoothly and was very polite. Pickup: Once onsite, I was the only customer and was assisted immediately. Dollar Rental has an automated Driver's License reader and touch screen for the paperwork portion of the process. While the automated "paperwork" was being completed, another employee pulled my rental car around front. The entire process from departing the shuttle to being inside the rental car took five minutes. Unheard of! Car: I reserved an economy car. It was in good condition. It was one of the new energy saving cars and I did notice the car rolled back a bit as if it were a stick shift if I did not keep my foot square on the brake. But other than that it was great. Most economy cars do not have automatic locks but this car did, plus it had Sirius radio. Special Surprise: On my way to return the car, my GPS didn't recognize the 100 Rental Blvd return address as indicated on the receipt which made me nervous since I was running late to catch my flight. Lo and behold, the directions to the rental car return area were securely fastened to the passenger side floor mats in large letters that could be read from the drivers' side seat. Ingenious! This was very helpful and unexpected. Return: The return process was simple and easy. Note: you must show your gas receipt upon returning the car. Shuttle and big kudos: As I mentioned, I was running late and I was concerned I would miss my flight. The shuttle pulled in as soon as I had returned the rental car and I informed the shuttle driver, Kenneth, of my concern and even though he thought I would arrive in plenty of time, he took my concerns seriously and insisted he would get me to the airport in time to catch my flight and he drove without hesitation and without making me wait for additional passengers. text: Here's the thing with Grimaldi's: many new Yorkers turn their noses at it because it's a major tourist attraction and because they've become a rapidly growing chain. Personally, these two things don't bother me at all. The original Grimaldi's down in Dumbo (Down under the Manhattan Bridge overpass) was at one time a favorite of mine until I took notice of inconsistency problems they began having. Because there is always such a heavy flow of customers, they have put far too many cooks in the kitchen. Sure, they're all using the same ingredients and following the same recipe, but pizza made by one man is simply not the same pizza as that made by another. That being said, I have been disappointed on multiple occasions at that location, and I have no interest in going out of my way to roll the dice. During my time spent in Tucson, however, I noticed a Grimaldi's out of the corner of my eye as I was driving home from a show put on by a local theater company. Having just eaten before the show, I wasn't particularly hungry, but out of shear surprise and curiosity I had to stop in. Upon entry, I was greeted at the door by the manager who told me to sit wherever I'd like. I took the bar, as the marble countertop and the fire from the brick oven called my name. The bartender took my order of a large pie and a cold Peroni, but being within earshot of my order, the pizza maker heard it and gave me a friendly "Coming right up!" As he was working the dough, he struck a pleasant conversation with me. He told me he was from Michigan and that he had always worked in pizza in some form or another. Before he started at Grimaldi's in Tucson, he had both prepared and delivered pizzas for years at various pizza joints around the Great Lakes. It was clear that the man new his stuff, so I had confidence that he'd fashion a respectable pie, but would it be as good as those I was accustomed to back home? The answer: every bit as good! In fact, I would go as far as to say that my pie was better than any Grimaldi's pie I've had in the Dumbo location. It was a fine example of Grimaldi's at its best, and it was sensational! Grimaldi's will no doubt continue to grow, but they need to pay close attention to quality control. They would be ashamed at themselves for letting their AZ location produce a better pie than their original. I'm still a fan of Grimaldi's pizza. It's not my favorite, but it's damn good! Count the stars, Yelpers!
